action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list.summary: List assets through the Asset Registry, including mounted plugin roots. Filter by classPaths (including subclasses), classFilter, nameRegex and skeletonPath. includeMetadata adds animation skeleton and playLength in seconds from registry tags without loading assets. Cursor-paginated with totalMatched, hasMore and nextCursor; maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

read_properties.summary: Read asset properties with values. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO (#568). propertyName accepts dotted/indexed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects (e.g. `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field`), and keyed paths that pick the one array element whose field equals a value (`Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`, reported back as indexedPath); landing on an array of subobjects also lists each element's index+class (#527). expandDepth inlines the properties of subobjects OWNED by this asset, so a data asset's nested payload comes back in ONE call instead of a reference you have to chase (#755); references to OTHER assets are marked expandable rather than followed, unless expandExternal=true. Capped by maxExpandedObjects with expansionTruncated reported.

list_properties.summary: List reflected properties on any asset.

get_properties.summary: Read property values on any asset; the same read as read_properties with includeValues on by default. propertyName accepts dotted/indexed/keyed paths into nested structs, array elements, and instanced subobjects, so one leaf of one element reads without dumping the array: `Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Offset.Scale3D`. valueFormat='json' returns structured values.

duplicate.summary: Duplicate any asset, including an Enhanced Input InputAction with independent copies of its instanced triggers, modifiers and PlayerMappableKeySettings. sourcePath and destinationPath name the assets; onConflict=error refuses an existing destination. Verify with gameplay(read_input_action). Rollback deletes the copy.

rename.summary: Rename asset: pass assetPath and newName, or sourcePath and destinationPath. World Partition levels are detected and their __ExternalActors__/__ExternalObjects__ packages migrate atomically alongside the .umap, source-side redirectors get fixed up, and the active editor world is swapped to blank if it matches the source (#409). Refuses if any package is dirty - save first. If a prior rename left externals orphaned at the old path, re-running reconciles them. Rollback descriptor is emitted even on partial failure so the inverse rename can recover. `force=true` lets the call merge into a destination with pre-existing externals (used by rollback). For batches of 3+ scene-referenced non-world assets use bulk_rename instead.

bulk_rename.summary: Batched rename using IAssetTools::RenameAssets. Each renames[] item is exactly one of {sourcePath, destinationPath (full package path with the asset name)}, {assetPath, newName} or {sourcePath, newPackagePath, newName}; an unknown or mixed key, or a destinationPath naming an existing folder, refuses the whole batch with invalidItems before anything moves (#1291). It runs as a single transaction with one redirector-fixup pass (matches Content Browser drag). Use this over looped rename for scene-referenced assets. World assets are rejected (status=rejected_world); use rename_asset which handles WP externals atomically (#409). The fix-up pass cannot see a referencer that is not loaded, so each renamed item reports redirectorLeft and the result carries redirectorsLeft/redirectorsRemoved plus redirectorPackages, which feeds straight into fixup_redirectors (#908). A batch that would leave another object of a multi-object package at the old path is refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind and splitPackages naming each one; nothing moves (#1137).

fixup_redirectors.summary: Clean up ObjectRedirectors left at the old paths after a move, bounded to exactly the packages you name. Preflights each redirector, its destination, and its hard AND soft referencers, then reports packagesToLoad/packagesToSave before touching anything; dryRun=true stops there. The real run loads only those referencers (a soft reference in an unloaded package is what the rename's own fix-up pass misses), rewrites them, saves them, RE-QUERIES the asset registry, and deletes a redirector only when nothing references it any more, reporting kept vs deleted per package with the referencers that survived. Naming a whole content root is refused unless allowProjectWide=true, so this can never turn into a project-wide resave. Protected mounts are refused outright. Runs unattended: it never calls the editor's interactive fix-up, so no 'No referencing assets found' message or Redirector Update Report modal can block it, and the result summarises fixed (redirectors whose referencers were all repointed), deleted, and noReferencers (#1266). dryRun is the way to preview; save=false repoints the referencers in memory without writing them and keeps every redirector they reference (#908).

move.summary: Move asset: pass sourcePath and destinationPath. The same call as rename.

delete.summary: Delete asset. force defaults to false and is a REAL guard: the bridge asks the Asset Registry for referencers first and refuses with success=false, reason='has_referencers' and the full referencers list rather than destroying an asset other packages point at (#976). force=true takes the force-delete path, which also auto-closes open asset editors (#278). On a delete the editor attempted and could not finish, the reason is open_in_editor / has_referencers / in_memory_referenced / package_read_only / package_dirty / unknown, with referencers, inMemoryReferencers, packageReadOnly and packageDirty diagnostics (#601).

delete_batch.summary: Batch-delete assets. Per-path status is deleted | absent | protected | refused | failed, plus reason+referencers on refused and failed entries. A referenced asset is refused per entry with force=false and the rest of the batch still runs, so one guarded asset never hides behind a bare failed count (#976, #278). Result carries deleted/absent/refused/failed/protected/total.

create_data_asset.summary: Create UDataAsset instance of custom class. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix (UMyConfig and MyConfig both resolve), a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name; a failed lookup lists the spellings tried and the closest matches (#823).

create_asset_by_class.summary: Create an asset of ANY concrete UObject class (not just UDataAsset) - physical-material subclasses, curves, settings objects. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix, a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a loaded class name (#823). Actors/components and specialized assets (Blueprint/Material) have dedicated actions (#726).

read_graph.summary: Read the NODE GRAPH of any EdGraph-backed asset: every graph in it, every node, and every node's pins with what each pin is connected to. Reflection cannot reach topology: UEdGraphNode declares its Pins array with no UPROPERTY, and UEdGraphPin is a plain class rather than a UObject, so no set_property, reflect_instance or find_object can read, break or make a connection (#1059). For the EdGraph types with no category of their own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them. A Blueprint, a PCG graph or a Material is REFUSED here and pointed at blueprint(read_graph) / blueprint(get_connections) / pcg(read_graph) / material(read_graph), which own those types and address them in their own terms. Each node reports name, path, class, title, position and comment; each pin reports name, pinId, direction, type, defaultValue and linkedTo[] naming the node and pin at the other end. Node settings themselves are read with reflection(action='reflect_instance') on the node path this returns, which already works; this reports what that cannot see. connectionCount is per graph and counts each wire once; nodesReported is how many nodes this call emitted, which maxNodes can cut below a graph's own nodeCount. A node reported with hasNoPins is broken: AllocateDefaultPins never ran for it, so it can never be wired and the editor cannot draw it. Each node also reports nodeGuid. To change the graph use connect_graph_pins, disconnect_graph_pins, add_graph_node and remove_graph_node, which go through the graph's own schema. An asset with no graph answers with an empty list and says so rather than failing.

connect_graph_pins.summary: Connect two pins in any EdGraph-backed asset with no category of its own, CustomizableObject (Mutable) among them, through the graph's own schema (TryCreateConnection), so the graph type's rules decide what is legal. A refusal returns the schema's own message with reason='schema_disallowed'. Address each end by node (nodeGuid, node path, name or unique title from read_graph) and pinId, which is the reliable form because pin names repeat on some node types; pin name plus direction also works. A pinId alone needs no node. brokenLinks lists any link the schema replaced. Rollback: disconnect_graph_pins. A Blueprint, Material or PCG graph is refused and pointed at its own category.

disconnect_graph_pins.summary: Break links in an EdGraph-backed asset through its schema. With a target pin, breaks that one link (BreakSinglePinLink); without one, breaks every link on the source pin (BreakPinLinks). Pins are addressed as in connect_graph_pins. A link that does not exist is reported with wasConnected=false and nothing changes. Rollback: connect_graph_pins when exactly one link was broken; otherwise brokenLinks names each one.

add_graph_node.summary: Add a node to an EdGraph-backed asset's graph through the schema's own node action, so its pins are allocated and it is parented to the graph. nodeClass is the class the action spawns (a CustomizableObjectNode class for Mutable, a SoundNode class for a SoundCue); actionName picks a menu entry by name ('category|name' also works) when several actions spawn the same class. When nothing matches, the error lists availableActions. spawnMode=direct constructs nodeClass itself (CreateNewGuid, PostPlacedNewNode, AllocateDefaultPins), and auto does that only for a schema that publishes no node actions. Returns nodeGuid, nodePath and every pin with its pinId. Rollback: remove_graph_node.

remove_graph_node.summary: Remove a node from an EdGraph-backed asset's graph: the schema breaks its links, then the node is destroyed. A node the graph type forbids deleting (a root or output node) is refused. brokenLinks names every link it had so they can be re-made. Rollback: add_graph_node with the same class and position when exactly one schema action spawns it (lossy: a fresh default node); otherwise rollbackPossible=false.

create_customizable_object.summary: Create a Mutable CustomizableObject through Mutable's own factory, so it holds its Source graph with the Base Object node and can be authored with add_graph_node and connect_graph_pins at once. An asset made with create_asset_by_class has no graph. Returns objectPath, graphName, rootNode (nodeGuid and pins with pinIds) and every graph node. onConflict=skip returns an existing CustomizableObject as existed; error refuses. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the plugin is off. Rollback: delete_asset.

compile_customizable_object.summary: Compile a Mutable CustomizableObject synchronously, without saving or gathering references, and report the outcome: state, compiled, and the LogMutable errors and warnings the compile wrote. A failed compile returns success=false with the first error. Fails with 'Mutable plugin not available' when the Mutable plugin is not enabled.

create_subobject.summary: Create a named subobject OWNED by an existing asset, inside that asset's package, and return its object path for later property writes. This is the missing half of editing a data asset whose payload is named subobjects referenced from a struct array: set_property, bulk_set_properties and append_array_elements can edit the entries, and this makes a new one. Component classes are accepted, unlike create_asset_by_class; Actors are refused because they are spawned into a level. className takes a /Script/Module.Class path, which is how you name a plugin class the Python `unreal` module never exposes. The new object is created RF_Standalone and the package is saved in the same call, so it survives the garbage collection that used to eat a fresh object within one call and is reachable by path from the next one. properties are applied to a throwaway instance first, so a bad path or value creates nothing. outer='asset' (default) gives '<asset>.<name>'; outer='package' puts it beside the asset in the package (#975).

bulk_upsert_data_assets.summary: Create or update up to 500 UDataAsset instances in ONE call. Every descriptor is first applied to a transient copy, so a bad class, property path, or value rejects the whole batch before a package is touched; nothing is half-written by a typo. Per-item status is created | updated | unchanged | skipped | failed (dryRun reports wouldCreate | wouldUpdate | wouldRemainUnchanged | wouldSkip), each with its own error when it failed. Replaying the same request returns unchanged, and only changed packages are saved. Emits a rollback descriptor that restores prior values and deletes what it created.

save.summary: Save one asset, exactly the packages named by assetPaths, or every dirty asset under /Game when both are omitted. assetPaths resolves each asset, object or package path to its loaded package (naming a World Partition actor names its external package), refuses the whole call before writing anything if one names nothing in memory, and reports each package as saved, notDirty or failed with a reason; no other package is written. The save-everything form refuses a call carrying any key it does not take, so a misspelt selector cannot widen it. force=true saves regardless of the dirty flag - several edits (OFPA level actors, some subsystem property writes) never mark their package dirty, so a dirty-only save skipped them and still reported success. Returns the package name plus on-disk file path, size and mtime so the write can be verified rather than trusted (#768). A failed save returns the engine's reason in error and saveDiagnostics, and when the engine refused a reference to a private object, illegalReference names that object, the object and property holding it, and how to clear it (#1120).

save_all_dirty.summary: Flush every dirty package to disk in one call. Reports the packages it attempted, which ones reached disk (with file path, size and mtime) and which are still dirty afterwards, because a bare savedAll boolean has come back true while packages were never written (#768).

set_mesh_material.summary: Assign material to static mesh slot.

set_mesh_materials_batch.summary: Assign materials across many meshes and slots in one call, so an N mesh x M slot kit costs one round trip instead of N*M. StaticMesh and SkeletalMesh both work. Address a slot by slotName (survives a reimport reordering slot indices) or by slotIndex (default 0); passing both is rejected when they disagree. Every submitted assignment returns its own index/ok/status/error, status being ok|updated|unchanged|invalid|protected|duplicate|not_found|slot_not_found|failed|skipped. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a mesh is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the assignments that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Each mesh is written and saved once no matter how many of its slots the batch names, and the rollback payload restores only the writes that landed (#822).

recenter_pivot.summary: Move static mesh pivot to geometry center. With assetPaths, the first mesh sets the reference pivot for all of them.

import_static_mesh.summary: Import from FBX, OBJ, or GLB/glTF (glTF routes through Interchange) (#549). importUniformScale=100 fixes metre-authored FBX (#687).

import_skeletal_mesh.summary: Import skeletal meshes with scale, replacement, target skeleton or a new skeleton, and optional material/texture import. importer=interchange supplies an explicit pipeline stack so UE 5.8 applies the settings; auto selects it on 5.8 and later. Legacy uses FbxImportUI. dryRun validates first; save defaults false. Returns importedAssets, meshes with bounds, material slots, skeleton and sockets, plus boxExtent, morphTargets and numLODs. Import changes may require backup restoration.

import_animation.summary: Import anim from FBX. importSettings sets any FbxAnimSequenceImportData or FbxImportUI field by UPROPERTY name or dotted path, e.g. {bSnapToClosestFrameBoundary: true} for clips whose length is not frame-aligned; a bool may drop its b prefix. An unknown key fails before anything is imported (#1134). filePaths imports a batch of FBX files into one folder with the same settings, one row per file under files. animations reads back each imported AnimSequence: path, playLength, numberOfFrames, numberOfKeys, frameRate, boneTrackCount, curveCount, enableRootMotion, and hasRootMotion with rootTravel from the root bone track (#1228).

import_file.summary: Import any source file through a chosen factory, unattended. factoryClass names a UFactory subclass by name or /Script path, including one a plugin ships (resolved at runtime; omit it to let the editor pick by extension). factoryProperties sets that factory's properties by UPROPERTY name or dotted path before the import runs, which is how a factory that raises its own options dialog is told to use the supplied options instead, since unattended mode cancels the dialog and the import with it. The file extension is checked against the factory's formats first. An unknown property fails before anything is imported (#1096). Imported assets are saved by default and imported[] reports saved, saveError or dirtyNotSaved per asset; save=false leaves them dirty (#1280).

import_font.summary: Import a .ttf/.otf (or .ttc/.otc collection) as a FontFace asset, with no import dialog. hinting and loadingPolicy set the face's own options; createFont=true also makes <name>_Font, a runtime Font whose Default typeface is this face. Returns path and the subFaces the file holds. onConflict: skip (default) | error | replace (reimport the bytes) (#1377).

create_font.summary: Create a runtime Font (composite font) whose default typeface has one entry per FontFace: fontFaces[] are FontFace asset paths and typefaceNames[] their entry names in the same order (Regular, Bold, Italic). This is the FTypefaceEntry/FFontData write Python cannot make. onConflict=update rewrites an existing font's default typeface and reports previousTypefaces (#1377).

import_texture.summary: Import image. sRGB/compressionSettings/lodGroup/neverStream are applied at import time (folded in, no second call needed) (#661).

create_render_target_2d.summary: Create and persist a TextureRenderTarget2D asset. Render format is applied before resource initialization.

generate_skeletal_mesh_lods.summary: Generate auto-reduced LODs on one SkeletalMesh, a list, or every SkeletalMesh in a folder, through the engine's RegenerateLOD (#1372). lodCount counts LOD 0; trianglePercentages gives each later LOD its triangle percentage of LOD 0, otherwise the engine's reduction settings apply. Idempotent: a mesh already at lodCount is skipped unless skipExisting=false, and a mesh with more LODs is never trimmed. Imported LODs are kept unless regenerateImported=true. dryRun reports without changing anything. Each mesh row lists every LOD with triangles, vertices, generated and trianglePercentage.

read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings.summary: Read a SkeletalMesh's per-LOD FSkeletalMeshBuildSettings without changing anything. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings (identical on a read), beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}, where each settings object carries bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bComputeWeightedNormals, bRemoveDegenerates, bUseHighPrecisionTangentBasis, bUseHighPrecisionSkinWeights, bUseFullPrecisionUVs, bUseBackwardsCompatibleF16TruncUVs, bOptimizeForInstancing, thresholdPosition, thresholdTangentNormal, thresholdUV, morphThresholdPosition and boneInfluenceLimit.

set_skeletal_mesh_optimize_for_instancin.summary: Write bOptimizeForInstancing on a SkeletalMesh's LOD build settings, which reorders the skin data so instanced draws of the mesh batch. Only LODs whose current value differs are touched, and the asset is only rebuilt and saved when at least one changes, so a call that asks for the value already set is a no-op. Read the current state with read_skeletal_mesh_build_settings first. lodIndex and allLods are mutually exclusive. Returns assetPath, lodCount and lods[] of {lodIndex, beforeBuildSettings, afterBuildSettings, beforeOptimizeForInstancing, afterOptimizeForInstancing, changed}.

get_static_mesh_build_settings.summary: Read a StaticMesh source model's FMeshBuildSettings (bRecomputeNormals, bRecomputeTangents, bUseMikkTSpace, bRemoveDegenerates, bGenerateLightmapUVs, BuildScale3D and every other field) by its engine property name. lodIndex picks the source model (default 0). Returns settings and sourceModelCount.

set_static_mesh_build_settings.summary: Write FMeshBuildSettings fields on a StaticMesh source model, then rebuild and save it. settings is keyed by engine property name, e.g. {bRecomputeNormals: true}; an unknown name or wrong type refuses the whole call before anything changes. A call that changes nothing skips the rebuild. Returns previous and settings, and rolls back to the previous values.

read_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights.summary: Read existing per-vertex skin influences from one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile. The caller must name 1-256 source MeshDescription vertex IDs, so a read cannot dump a whole mesh. Each influence returns boneName, boneIndex, normalized weight and exact uint16 rawWeight. Render data may use 8-bit weights unless high-precision skin weights are enabled. Generated LODs without source geometry are refused.

read_skeletal_mesh_bone_vertex_bounds.summary: Measure where each bone's skinned vertices sit on one SkeletalMesh source LOD and profile, so physics bodies, sockets and hit volumes can be sized from the mesh instead of guessed. By default each source vertex counts once, for its dominant bone; minWeight counts it for every bone weighing at least that much. boneNames limits the report to those bones (a named bone with no vertices comes back with vertexCount 0); omitted, every bone that owns a vertex is listed. Each bone returns boneName, boneIndex, parentName, vertexCount, bindPose (its component-space reference transform), componentSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bind pose and boneSpace {min, max, center, extent} in the bone's own bind-pose frame, the frame a physics body on that bone uses. Also returns vertexCount, unweightedVertexCount and, with minWeight, belowThresholdVertexCount. Read-only.

set_skeletal_mesh_skin_weights.summary: Replace skin influences on explicitly selected source MeshDescription vertices in one existing SkeletalMesh LOD/profile. The complete batch is validated before mutation: invalid or duplicate vertices/bones, non-finite/negative/out-of-range weights and all-zero sets fail without a write. Unreal's FBoneWeights normalizes, quantizes to uint16 source weights and prunes ordinary edits to its influence limit; actual before/after values are read back. Other source vertices and source profiles are untouched. Rebuilding may refresh derived render data and dependent generated LODs. A changed mesh is rebuilt and saved; an identical request is a no-op. Rollback payloads use restoreRawWeights with exact uint16 rawWeight values.

read_cloth_data.summary: Read Chaos cloth data on a skeletal mesh: per clothing asset, its configs (reflected properties), LOD count, and per-LOD point-weight-map summary (name, target, vertex count, min/max - including the MaxDistances mask). Also reports which render sections each clothing asset is bound to (boundSections, bound), every section of every LOD (sections: lodIndex, sectionIndex, materialIndex, usesCloth, clothingAsset, assetLodIndex) and unboundClothingAssets: an asset bound to no section never simulates (#595/#1139).

bind_cloth_to_section.summary: Bind a clothing asset to one render section so it simulates, as the skeletal mesh editor's section clothing dropdown does. Whatever the section was bound to is unbound first. lodIndex and sectionIndex are validated against the mesh, assetLodIndex against the clothing asset. Saves the mesh; rolls back to the previous binding (#1139).

unbind_cloth_from_section.summary: Remove the clothing asset bound to one render section. The engine unbinds per LOD, so other sections of that LOD bound to the same asset are released too and listed in releasedSections. A section with no binding is a no-op. Saves the mesh; rolls back by rebinding (#1139).

set_cloth_config.summary: Set properties on a clothing asset's Chaos cloth config via reflection (#595).

export_texture.summary: Export a Texture2D to a PNG on disk (for inspection or external diffing) (#697).

compare_textures.summary: Compare two Texture2D assets by dimensions, pixel format, and source-content identity (FTextureSource id) - tells you whether an authored texture actually changed without offline pixel-diffing (#697).

import_texture_batch.summary: Batch import PNGs and other images with per-file preset=normal|masks|color and settings. Normal maps use linear Normalmap compression without green flip; packed masks use linear Masks; color uses sRGB. Per-file lodGroup, maxTextureSize, compressionSettings, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel override presets. All entries preflight before import; dryRun writes nothing. Saves after applying settings and returns per-item importedAssets, readBack and saved. Rollback deletes new textures only; replaced pixels require a backup.

reimport.summary: Reimport an imported asset from its source file, or from filePath, which is recorded as its new source. A texture keeps its settings: compression, LOD group, sRGB, NeverStream, max size, mip generation, filter and addressing are read before the reimport and any the reimport changed are put back (preserveSettings=false skips that). For a texture the response carries settingsBefore, settingsAfter, restoredSettings (what the reimport changed and was undone) and sourceSizeBefore/sourceSizeAfter, the source pixel dimensions. The package is left dirty and unsaved unless save=true; packageDirty reports it.

read_datatable.summary: Read DataTable rows as structured JSON (struct fields come back as objects). rowNames returns exactly the named rows in the order given, matched like FindRow (case-insensitive), and lists names the table lacks in missingRowNames instead of failing; rowFilter is a substring match instead. columns narrows each row to its Name and the named top-level row-struct fields, which is how one field is read across every row of a wide table; an unknown name is refused with the row struct's field list, and the response echoes the resolved columns. A large table overflows the response inline: pass outputPath to write the rows (after rowNames, rowFilter and columns) to a file as a JSON array instead. The response then carries outputPath (resolved absolute path), rowCount, bytes, rowStruct and totalRowCount, with no rows or rowNames. A relative outputPath resolves under the project's Saved/, missing folders are created and an existing file is overwritten.

clone_datatable_rows.summary: Clone DataTable rows in one call: clones=[{sourceRow, rowName, overrides?}]. Copies native row memory before applying nested or dotted struct overrides, preserving omitted fields and references. All source rows must exist and all destination names must be unused; the full batch is validated before mutation. dryRun returns proposedRows; writes return rows with fields read back, clonedCount, rowCount, saved and persisted. Uses one editor undo transaction; rollback removes the cloned rows with the same save policy and is marked lossy because row change hook side effects cannot be reversed.

set_datatable_row.summary: Append or overwrite a single DataTable row. row carries row-struct fields, and a partial update merges with the existing row. Idempotent; rollback restores the prior row (#437).

update_datatable_row.summary: Alias for set_datatable_row; partial update merges with existing row (#437).

remove_datatable_row.summary: Remove a DataTable row with rowName, or several with rowNames in one transaction. Idempotent: alreadyDeleted=true when all selected rows are absent. save defaults to true; save=false keeps removal in memory, including clone_datatable_rows rollback. Batch or unsaved removal uses editor undo to restore row values; the original single saved removal returns its set_datatable_row inverse.

get_datatable_row.summary: Read one DataTable row's fields without dumping the whole table (#535).

set_datatable_cell.summary: Write a single field on a single existing row (merges, leaves other cells untouched). Errors if the row doesn't exist (#535).

set_datatable_cells.summary: Write many cells across many existing rows in one call, such as relabelling one column on every row. Every cell is validated first (the row exists, the column is a top-level field, the value parses as set_datatable_cell parses it); if any fails, nothing is written and errors[] lists each failing cell. The rest apply in one undo transaction with one Modify/PostEditChange, then every row is re-exported and compared with the export taken before: touched rows may differ only in the requested fields and every other row must be identical, or the write is rolled back and the offending row and field named. Reports changedCells, unchangedCells (already equal), rowsTouched and verified. dryRun validates and reports without writing; save defaults to false; rollback restores the prior values.

rename_datatable_row.summary: Rename a row key, preserving its values (#535).

fill_datatable_from_json.summary: Bulk-upsert rows from a {rowName: {field: value}} object without touching unrelated rows (non-destructive, unlike reimport_datatable) (#535).

import_curvetable.summary: Import CurveTable from JSON/CSV string or file.

remove_curvetable_row.summary: Remove CurveTable row. Idempotent if missing.

get_curvetable_keys.summary: Read keys from one CurveTable row.

set_curvetable_keys.summary: Replace keys on one CurveTable row.

add_curvetable_key.summary: Add or update one key on a CurveTable row.

list_textures.summary: List textures, cursor-paginated. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

get_texture_info.summary: Read one texture or many via assetPaths: dimensions, MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream, flipGreenChannel, mip count and pixel format.

set_texture_settings.summary: Set one texture or many via assetPaths, with preset=normal|masks|color and explicit settings. Supports MaxTextureSize (maxTextureSize), compressionSettings including Masks, lodGroup, sRGB, neverStream and flipGreenChannel. Validates every texture before mutation; dryRun previews, save defaults false. Returns previousSettings and readBack per texture, saved, and a rollback restoring the previous settings.

set_stringtable_entry.summary: Create or update one StringTable entry. Pass sourceString, or value as a second spelling of it.

remove_stringtable_entry.summary: Remove one StringTable entry. Idempotent (alreadyDeleted=true if missing).

import_stringtable_csv.summary: Import or refresh a String Table from a CSV that is the canonical source, using Unreal's own String Table CSV importer. The CSV is parsed into a throwaway table and checked against expectedKeys FIRST, so a malformed file or a key set that does not match leaves the asset untouched and comes back with missingKeys/unexpectedKeys instead. replaceExisting=true prunes entries the CSV no longer carries, which is what makes the CSV canonical rather than additive; the prune runs after a successful merge so a bad parse can never empty the table. Returns addedKeys, updatedKeys, removedKeys, entry counts and an explicit persisted/saved plus persistError, so a write that did not reach disk is never reported as a success. A relative csvPath is read against the project directory (#978).

add_input_mapping.summary: Append an Enhanced Input key mapping to an InputMappingContext (InputAction + key by name string e.g. 'Mouse2D','LeftMouseButton'). Idempotent on (action,key). For modifiers/triggers use gameplay(set_mapping_modifiers). Same as gameplay(add_imc_mapping) (#525). Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted.

remove_input_mapping.summary: Remove an IMC key mapping. Same as gameplay(remove_imc_mapping) (#525). Returns saved, persisted, packageDirty, packageName, and persistError when not persisted.

list_input_mappings.summary: List an IMC's key->action bindings with triggers/modifiers, each with its class and property values (Negate X/Y/Z, SwizzleAxis Order). Same as gameplay(read_imc) (#525).

add_socket.summary: Add socket to StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. SkeletalMesh writes mesh-local sockets by default; pass a Skeleton asset path to edit skeleton-level sockets. Idempotent on socket name; pass onConflict='update' to overwrite an existing socket's transform with the supplied relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale (#412).

list_sockets.summary: List sockets on a mesh (StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh). SkeletalMesh results include mesh-local sockets plus assigned Skeleton sockets, each with source='mesh' or source='skeleton'. Every skeletal socket also carries componentTransform {location, rotation, scale}: its transform in component space at the reference pose (the SkeletalMesh's pose for a mesh, including its Skeleton's sockets; the Skeleton's own for a Skeleton asset, named in componentTransformPose), so no actor is needed to see where a socket sits. A socket whose bone is missing from that skeleton returns componentTransformError instead.

set_socket_transform.summary: Update an existing socket's relative transform on StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh. Pass any subset of relativeLocation/relativeRotation/relativeScale; omitted fields stay at their current values. Errors if the socket does not exist (use add_socket to create). Common after FBX import when SOCKET_* empties land with scale=(100,100,100) (#412).

set_property.summary: Assign a different skeleton to an existing SkeletalMesh with propertyName=Skeleton and value set to the skeleton object path; save controls persistence. Use edit_collection_entry to clone a keyed array element or patch one TMap entry. Set a UPROPERTY on any loaded asset (Material, DataAsset, DataTable, SubsurfaceProfile, etc.) using a dotted path. Blueprint paths resolve to the generated-class CDO so you can author its defaults + Instanced sub-object arrays (#568). Walks nested structs, array elements by index (`Rules[1]`) or by key (`Rules[Id=Axe]`: exactly one element's Id must equal Axe, else the error lists the ids), and instanced subobjects internally - no more read-modify-write copies (e.g. `settings.mean_free_path_distance` on a UMaterial, or `Config.Traits[1].Params.Field` on a config asset #527). Value goes through MCPJsonProperty::SetJsonOnProperty so JSON null clears object refs, structs accept {x,y,z}, arrays/maps round-trip. TMap values take { "Key": value } or, for struct keys, [{ key: {...}, value: ... }]; a write that cannot store every entry fails and leaves the old value untouched (#820). The write is saved to the package by default and the result reports persisted plus the package name; a write that could not reach disk (save=false, a protected mount, a read-only file, a refused save) comes back with persisted=false and persistError naming the reason instead of a bare success that reverts on the next editor start (#931) (#420). With save=false, nested array field writes stay in memory, leave the package dirty, and support editor undo; rollback restores the old value with the same save option. An Instanced or EditInlineNew object property takes {instanceClass, properties}: a new subobject of that class is created with the owning object as its outer and its fields set from properties, e.g. RootMotionModifier = {instanceClass: "RootMotionModifier_Scale", properties: {Scale: {x:0,y:0,z:0}}} (#1292). An array of structs is written whole or per element (PropTypes[1].Modes = [{Key, DisplayName, bInCycle}, ...]); struct members match by C++ name, display name, or the Python spelling (display_name, in_cycle) (#1370).

edit_collection_entry.summary: Update or clone one struct array element or TMap entry on a data asset, selected by entryKey. Arrays also need keyField (for example WeaponId); maps use their actual reflected key type. newKey clones to an unused key, while omitting it patches the existing entry. overrides accepts nested objects and dotted struct fields, preserving omitted fields. Validates before mutation; duplicate or missing keys fail. dryRun returns proposedValue; writes return value read back, count, saved and persisted. Rollback restores the whole collection, so replay before further collection edits. Instanced subobject cloning is refused.

append_array_elements.summary: Append one or more JSON values to a reflected TArray without replacing existing entries. Supports dotted property paths plus native and user-defined USTRUCT elements. All elements are validated before mutation; returns appended indices and rollback data. The append is saved to the package by default and reports persisted / persistError the same way set_property does (#931); rollback preserves the same save option, so an unsaved append can be restored without writing to disk.

bulk_set_properties.summary: Set dotted UPROPERTY paths (indexed `Rules[1].X` or keyed `Rules[Id=Axe].X`, keys matched once in preflight) on as many as 500 assets in one preflighted batch. Every asset, path, and value is validated before anything is mutated, and every submitted item comes back with its own ok/status/error, so a bad path in item 300 never hides the other 499 verdicts. Default is all-or-nothing: any preflight rejection aborts before a single UObject is touched. Pass continueOnError to apply the items that did pass and keep the rejects reported alongside them. Returns per-property readback, aggregate counts, targeted save results, and a replayable rollback payload covering only the writes that landed.

bulk_read_properties.summary: Read the SAME properties off many assets in one call, filtered and aggregated in the editor. read_properties answers one asset per call, which turns a library-wide question (concurrency settings across 582 sound assets, cull distances across 201 foliage types) into a loop. Select with assetPaths or with directory narrowed by classNames; propertyNames accepts dotted paths into nested structs (e.g. 'CullDistance.Max'), and a Blueprint path reads its generated-class CDO. Predicates, groupBy and countBy all evaluate here: filtering happens before anything crosses the wire, with the same operators as level(query_components). Absent and null are reported separately, because 'this class has no such property' and 'this property is unset' are different findings; suspect is true for either, and suspectOnly returns just those rows. Never writes, and reports dirtiedPackages (#909).

set_texture_settings_by_type.summary: Apply the canonical (compressionSettings, sRGB, LOD group) combo to every texture in each group: normal -> Normalmap, grayscale -> Grayscale, baseColor -> Default sRGB, hdr -> HDR (#421).

create_interchange_pipeline.summary: One-call factory for a UInterchangeGenericAssetsPipeline asset with the 15-property mesh-import boilerplate already applied (RecomputeNormals=false, MikkTSpace=true, HighPrecisionTangents=true, BuildNanite=false, CreatePhysicsAsset=false, etc.) (#421).

reload_package.summary: Force reload an asset package from disk.

health_check.summary: Diagnose stuck-unloadable asset. Returns onDisk/inRegistry/isLoaded/canLoad/isStuck flags so an agent can detect the half-shutdown state where load returns null but the file exists (#279).

force_reload.summary: Aggressive reload from disk: closes open editors, reloads the package (rebuilding a Blueprint's class and CDO so container properties come back fresh, not just scalars), and reports objectReplaced. Refuses a dirty package unless discardUnsaved=true, and fails loudly when the editor would not release the old object rather than serving stale values (#279/#820).

export.summary: Export static or skeletal meshes to FBX, Texture2D to PNG, or MaterialInstance parameters to JSON for a DCC round-trip. Material JSON includes parent lineage, scalar/vector/texture overrides and resolved parameter values. DataTable and CompositeDataTable require .json or .csv; format overrides their serializer. Relative outputPath resolves against the project directory; missing folders are created. replaceExisting defaults true; dryRun writes no file. Returns outputPath, assetClass, bytes, and material readBack or table rowCount. Overwritten files require a backup.

search_fts.summary: Ranked asset search (token-scored over name/class/path). Every match is scored and the ranked list is paged, so the top page is a page rather than the whole answer. maxResults is a deprecated spelling of limit.

reindex_fts.summary: Rescan a content path so newly added assets on disk become searchable by search_fts.

get_referencers.summary: Batch reverse dependency lookup for packages (or one packagePath). includeDetails follows Blueprint referencers up to maxDepth and reports maps, external actor packages, Blueprint paths and one shortest route per package. includeMeshInfo adds bounds, material slots, skeleton, sockets and static mesh collision setup. Returns referencersByPackage and detailsByPackage. Uses saved registry references; runtime-only and unsaved references are outside its scope.

get_dependencies.summary: Forward dependency lookup (what packages this asset references) (#588). Returns {dependenciesByPackage, totalDependencies}.

list_skeleton_bones.summary: List bones (names + rest-pose local and component-space transforms) from a SkeletalMesh or Skeleton asset, no live actor needed (#593). Returns {bones, boneCount, sourceKind, scaleSummary}. scaleSummary covers every bone whatever the page: bonesWithNonUnitLocalScale, min/maxComponentScale, rootScale and up to 32 scaledBones. limit pages the bones and offset starts the page; nextOffset is set while more remain. includeBones=false returns the summary alone (#1201).

get_primary_asset_ids.summary: Enumerate AssetManager-registered FPrimaryAssetIds (verify a primary-asset registration) (#579). Returns {primaryAssetIds:[{primaryAssetId, type, name, assetPath}], count, total}.

set_sk_material_slots.summary: Set materials on a USkeletalMesh by slot name or slotIndex (bypasses the blueprint override-materials path that UE's ICH silently reverts).

diagnose_registry.summary: Scan a content path and compare disk vs AssetRegistry (including in-memory pending-kill entries). Returns onDiskCount, inMemoryIncludedCount, ghostCount and paths.

get_mesh_bounds.summary: Get StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh bounding box. Returns min, max, boxExtent, boxCenter, meshKind (#193/#351).

get_mesh_info.summary: One-call static or skeletal mesh summary: boundsOrigin, boundsExtent, materialSlots (index, slotName, materialPath, isDefaultFallback), sockets (mesh and skeleton sockets), socketCount, skeletonPath, LOD/vertex counts and heightM.

read_import_sources.summary: Read AssetImportData source filenames on an imported asset (StaticMesh, SkeletalMesh, Texture, Animation, etc.). Returns sources[] of {relativeFilename, absolutePath, timestamp, fileHash, displayLabelName} (#270).

get_mesh_collision.summary: Inspect StaticMesh collision setup. Returns collisionTraceFlag, hasSimple/ComplexCollision, element counts (#177).

get_mesh_geometry.summary: Read actual vertex data off a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh: per-section positions, uvs, normals and triangle indices, from the engine's render data (no ProceduralMeshComponent plugin needed). Triangle indices are section-local, so they index that section's own positions array; add baseVertexIndex for LOD-global indices. Over 20000 vertices inline is refused - pass dumpToFile to write the full data to a JSON file instead, or narrow with sectionIndex (#948/#926/#953).

measure_mesh_geometry.summary: Measure a StaticMesh OR SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, dimensions, surfaceArea, volume, triangleCount, vertexCount, isClosed, isManifold, boundaryEdgeCount, nonManifoldEdgeCount. surfaceArea and volume are NAMED fields, never a positional pair (the engine's get_mesh_volume_area returns them in the order opposite to its name, #938). Vertices are welded by position before topology analysis so a UV seam does not read as a hole (#938/#953).

read_uv_channels.summary: Report every UV channel of a StaticMesh or SkeletalMesh LOD: bounds, UV area, unit-square coverage, overlap fraction and the triangles involved, island count, degenerate islands, seam edges, out-of-range and flipped triangles, plus which channel LightMapCoordinateIndex points at and the LOD's lightmap build settings. This is the verification half of the UV surface: every other UV action reports the same channel block after it writes, so a change can be checked rather than trusted. Overlap and coverage are RASTERISED at rasterSize rather than tested exactly, and the result says so via overlapMethod.

set_uv_channel_count.summary: Add, remove, resize or copy a UV channel. Channel count is a mesh-description attribute with no UPROPERTY, so asset(set_property) cannot reach it. Setting the count it already has returns existed=true and skips the rebuild. Growing has an exact inverse and the rollback restores it; remove and copy-over-existing DESTROY coordinates, so those report rollbackRestoresChannelCountOnly rather than pretending the undo is complete.

unwrap_uvs.summary: Auto-unwrap and pack islands into one channel via Geometry Script, adding the channel if it does not exist. It converts the LOD to a DynamicMesh and back, so the WHOLE LOD is rewritten rather than only its UVs; the result says so. Pass backupToChannel for a lossless rollback, otherwise only the channel count is restorable. Without the Geometry Script plugin it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable instead of failing opaquely.

transform_uvs.summary: One action for every UV transform: the whole channel, chosen islands, triangles facing a direction, or one material slot, plus flips. The filter is the only thing that varies, so the maths lives in one place rather than in four near-identical actions. Edits the mesh description directly, touching nothing but the UV channel, and emits an EXACT inverse as its rollback. A zero scale component is refused because it has no inverse; an identity transform returns existed=true without rebuilding.

generate_lightmap_uvs.summary: Apply the lightmap build settings AND run UStaticMesh::Build AND read the result back. Deliberately not a setter: bGenerateLightmapUVs, SrcLightmapIndex, DstLightmapIndex and LightMapCoordinateIndex are plain UPROPERTYs that asset(set_property) already writes, and writing them does NOTHING until the mesh rebuilds. That rebuild is the whole point. Returns the channel the build actually produced with its overlap and island report, and fails loudly when the channel did not appear. StaticMesh only. Rollback restores the settings, not the generated coordinates.

export_uv_layout.summary: Render one UV channel to a PNG under Saved/UVLayouts: white wireframe, one hue per island, red where two triangles share a texel, yellow unit-square border. Returns the file path plus the same channel statistics read_uv_channels reports, so the picture and the numbers describe the same rasterisation. Use it to SEE why a lightmap bake is wrong instead of inferring it from counts.

check_uvs.summary: One-call UV health report, the same idiom as measure_mesh_geometry. Flags a missing lightmap channel, a LightMapCoordinateIndex that disagrees with the build's DstLightmapIndex, overlap in the lightmap channel over budget, lightmap UVs outside 0..1, empty or degenerate channels and islands, and flipped triangles, each with a severity and the action that fixes it. Out-of-range UVs OUTSIDE the lightmap channel are reported as info rather than a fault, because tiling is legitimate there.

apply_mesh_simplify.summary: Reduce a StaticMesh's triangle count while keeping its silhouette, through Geometry Script. Nine strategies because 'simplify' means different things: a target triangleCount or vertexCount, a geometric tolerance (the furthest the surface may drift), an edgeLength, a fast cluster-based edgeLength, a structural collapse of coplanar regions (planar) or of PolyGroup faces (polygroup), and the editor's own reducer (editorTriangleCount, editorVertexCount). NOT reachable through asset(set_property): a StaticMesh's LOD reduction settings build a NEW LOD, they never rewrite LOD 0's source geometry, and no UPROPERTY means 'collapse this mesh to 500 triangles'. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default (outputPath, or '<assetPath>_Simplified'), whose rollback is a complete delete; inPlace=true overwrites the source and reports that its edit has no inverse, with backupPath as the escape. Idempotent: a mesh already at or under the target reports changed=false and is not rewritten. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin, and without it returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable.

apply_mesh_remesh.summary: Rebuild a StaticMesh's triangulation at a uniform or adaptive density. Different from apply_mesh_simplify: simplify only removes triangles, remesh splits AND collapses AND flips edges to reach an even edge length, which is what a mesh needs before deformation, baking, or a convex decomposition that would otherwise follow the original triangulation's bias. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Remeshed'). Deliberately NOT idempotent and says so in repeatIsIdempotent: remeshing a remeshed mesh keeps moving vertices, so a repeat is a second edit rather than a no-op, which is why the separate-output default matters here more than anywhere else. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

apply_mesh_mirror.summary: Reflect a StaticMesh across a plane, optionally cutting away the far side first and welding the seam. This is the 'model half of it and mirror' workflow, and it is real geometry rather than a negative component scale, which inverts the winding and lights wrong; no UPROPERTY on a StaticMesh mirrors its source geometry. Name the plane with axis=x|y|z through planeOrigin, or axis=custom with an explicit planeNormal. Writes a SEPARATE asset by default ('<assetPath>_Mirrored'). NOT idempotent and says so: mirroring a mirrored mesh doubles it again rather than returning the original. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

apply_mesh_hole_fill.summary: Close every open boundary loop on a StaticMesh so it becomes watertight, which is what a boolean, a voxel operation, a convex decomposition and a physics conversion all require and the most common reason those fail. WELDS FIRST by default: a great many 'holes' are not holes but duplicated vertices along a seam that no fill can close, and running the fill alone on such a mesh reports zero holes filled while the mesh stays open. Genuinely idempotent: a mesh with nothing left to fill reports existed=true and is not rewritten. Reports filledHoles, failedHoleFills, weldedOpenEdges and the before/after open-border-edge counts, so 'watertight now' can be verified rather than assumed. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin.

generate_mesh_collision.summary: Build simple collision shapes for a StaticMesh from its own geometry, or clear them. Eight methods from axis-aligned boxes to a full convex decomposition. NOT reachable through asset(set_property): UBodySetup AggGeom is a UPROPERTY, but what has to go into it is the OUTPUT of a decomposition solver running over the mesh, and there is no value a caller could supply; the shape count and trace flag stay ordinary property writes and asset(get_mesh_collision) is still the read half. Idempotent: generation from the same mesh with the same options is deterministic, so a repeat reports changed=false without rewriting the asset, compared by a structural signature (shape counts per kind, hull vertex counts, trace flag) rather than byte-for-byte. op='clear' is the remove half and needs no plugin at all. A generation that produces zero shapes is reported as a failure naming apply_mesh_hole_fill, not as a success that quietly left the mesh with no collision.

apply_mesh_fracture.summary: Cut a StaticMesh with planes and write each resulting piece out as its own StaticMesh asset, ready to be placed, simulated or destroyed individually. Three patterns: slice (parallel cuts along one axis), grid (cuts along all three) and random (seeded planes through the bounds). WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not Chaos destruction and produces no UGeometryCollection, because every engine entry point for that carries no UFUNCTION and reflection cannot reach it; the result says so in producesGeometryCollection=false rather than leaving it to be discovered. The source asset is never modified, so the rollback is an exact delete of the pieces it wrote. Seeded, therefore repeatable: onConflict='error' (the default) refuses rather than writing over pieces already there. dryRun lists the cut planes and every path it would write.

audit_hygiene.summary: One read-only sweep answering the questions a project accumulates answers to and never gets asked: what nothing references (unreferenced), what references nothing (brokenReferences), what exists twice (duplicates), what breaks the naming convention (naming), and what renames left behind (redirectors). asset(get_referencers) and asset(get_dependencies) answer the first two for ONE named package; this is the project-wide form, which is the one an agent needs. The unreferenced section carries a caveat to read before acting on it: an asset loaded by name from an INI setting, from C++ with a hardcoded path, or from a soft reference resolved at runtime has no package dependency and appears there while being very much in use, so treat it as candidates to review rather than a delete list. Maps, World Partition external actors and Asset Manager primary assets are already excluded for that reason. Duplicate detection by content matches class, file size and saved package hash, which finds a file copied verbatim but NOT a copy saved under a different name (the name is inside the file); duplicateMethod='name' is what catches an asset imported twice into two folders. Naming rules match on the asset's class name, so WidgetBlueprint and AnimBlueprint carry their own prefixes rather than inheriting Blueprint's, and the effective table comes back in rulesApplied. Counts are always complete; only the listings are capped by maxIssues.

bulk_fix_hygiene.summary: The batched fix-up for the two audit_hygiene findings a machine can act on without deciding something a person should: a name that breaks the convention (fix='naming') and an asset nothing references (fix='unreferenced'). Same preflight shape as bulk_set_properties: every candidate is validated, every candidate gets a status back including the rejected ones, and a failed preflight aborts before anything is touched unless continueOnError. THREE SAFETY RULES that are not the shape: dryRun DEFAULTS TO TRUE and the dry run names every asset with its exact destination; fix='unreferenced' MOVES assets into quarantineFolder by default rather than deleting them, and that move has an exact inverse this call emits as its rollback; and findings are recomputed here rather than taken from an audit, so an asset that gained a referencer since then is skipped with the referencer named. maxFixes caps the batch far below the audit's scan ceiling. Worlds are refused outright, because moving one without migrating its external-actor packages in the same batch orphans every actor in the level; use asset(rename). fix='redirectors' is refused too and points at asset(fixup_redirectors), which already does it properly.

mesh_boolean.summary: Boolean CSG between two StaticMeshes: union, subtract, intersect, trimInside, trimOutside, newPolyGroupInside, newPolyGroupOutside. The target is the mesh being cut and the tool is what cuts it, each placed by its own optional transform. Writes to a SEPARATE output asset by default (outputPath, or '<targetPath>_<Operation>' when omitted); inPlace=true opts into overwriting the target and is the only destructive form. An existing outputPath is refused unless onConflict='replace'. An empty result is refused and nothing is written unless allowEmptyResult=true, because two meshes that never overlap otherwise report success having deleted everything. Returns triangle and vertex counts for both inputs and the result, plus the written asset's triangles, vertices, LOD count, material slots and bounds, so the operation can be verified rather than trusted. dryRun runs the boolean and reports those counts without writing. Materials and simple collision are copied from the target by default. Needs the Geometry Script engine plugin: without it the call returns reason='geometry_scripting_unavailable' naming what to enable, rather than failing opaquely (#916).

move_folder.summary: Move/rename entire content folder with redirector fixup in one transaction. Refused with reason=package_objects_left_behind, before anything moves, when a package in the folder holds an object the move would leave at the old path (#1137) (#192).

create_folder.summary: Create empty content browser folder(s); path and paths combine. Returns per-path created/existed/failed (#212).

delete_folder.summary: Delete content browser folder(s) - counterpart to delete_asset, which leaves the parent directory entry behind as an orphan. Empty folders only by default; pass force=true to also delete any assets still inside (Content Browser 'Delete folder' equivalent). A World Partition map's __ExternalActors__ and __ExternalObjects__ packages for the folder go with it and are counted in externalPackagesDeleted; packages still loaded are kept and reported. Per-path status (deleted/absent/failed) with reason (invalid_path/protected_path/not_empty/delete_failed) and a sample of contained assets on not_empty entries.

create_user_defined_enum.summary: Create a UserDefinedEnum content asset, optionally pre-populated with values (#686).

list_enum_values.summary: List a UEnum's enumerators (index, authored short name, display name, value). Works on native and UserDefinedEnum assets (#686).

edit_user_defined_enum.summary: Author a UserDefinedEnum content asset. op=add_value appends an enumerator (authored name is auto-assigned; pass displayName - or name - to set the editable display text). op=rename_value sets a new displayName on the enumerator resolved by index or name (matches short or display name). op=remove_value deletes it. Recompiles dependents automatically. Native UEnums are not editable (#686).

create_user_defined_struct.summary: Create a UserDefinedStruct content asset, optionally pre-populated with fields (#735).

list_struct_fields.summary: List a UserDefinedStruct's members (index, internal name, friendly/display name, GUID, type label, and typeSpec, which add_field and set_field_type accept back). Use this to find the GUID for a stable rename/retype. Native structs are not editable (#735).

edit_user_defined_struct.summary: Author a UserDefinedStruct content asset. op=add_field appends a member (pass fieldName for its display name; type accepts scalars, structs, enums, object refs and containers such as struct:/Game/S.S[], TArray<int>, Set<Name>, Map<Name,int>, and a field typeSpec from list_struct_fields round-trips). op=rename_field sets a new newDisplayName on the member resolved by fieldGuid or fieldName - the member GUID is preserved so existing Blueprint pins and DataTable rows survive. op=set_field_type changes a member's type. op=remove_field deletes it. add_field, set_field_type and remove_field recompile every loaded Blueprint whose class holds the struct, reinstancing its live instances, and list them in dependentsRecompiled. Native structs are not editable (#735).

rename_struct_field.summary: Rename a UserDefinedStruct field's display name while preserving its member GUID, so Blueprint pins and DataTable rows keyed off it survive. The same edit as edit_user_defined_struct(op=rename_field). fieldName matches the friendly or internal name (#735).

list_locks.summary: List all currently-held asset locks with holder session id, acquiredAt, and ttlSecondsRemaining.

diff.summary: Semantic structural diff between two assets, dispatching on the asset's class. Blueprints: parent class, variables, functions, components, per-graph node and connection deltas. Skeleton and SkeletalMesh: raw bone additions and removals, reparenting (bone, fromParent, toParent), raw-index changes (bone, fromIndex, toIndex), and declared virtual-bone additions and removals, with hierarchyCompatible and editorCompatible reported SEPARATELY. That separation is the point: it answers whether two skeletons are bone-compatible enough to register as Compatible Skeletons or whether a retarget is required, because appending bones (virtual ones especially) leaves the shared hierarchy intact while reparenting an existing bone does not (#879). Deliberately OUT of scope and reported as such: reference-pose transforms (referencePoseCompared=false), export names (exportNamesCompared=false), sockets and retarget sources; structureScope spells the boundary out in the result. Both paths must be the same class. Other asset types report that diffing is not supported yet rather than failing opaquely.

epic_add_key.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Adds a key to a row. Params: curve_table, row_name, key

epic_add_row.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Adds a new row to the curve table with an optional default value. Params: curve_table, row_name, default_value?

epic_add_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Adds new rows with default values to the data table. Params: data_table, row_names

epic_create__data_asset_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_asset.DataAssetTools] Creates a new DataAsset asset in the project. Params: folder_path, asset_name, asset_type

epic_create__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Creates a new DataTable asset with the specified column schema. Params: folder_path, asset_name, schema

epic_create__string_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Creates a new StringTable asset. Params: folder_path, asset_name

epic_create_folder.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Creates a folder at the specified path. Params: path

epic_delete.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Deletes an asset or folder. Params: path

epic_duplicate.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Makes a copy of a folder or asset. Params: path, new_path

epic_exists.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Determines if a folder or asset exists. Params: path

epic_find_assets.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Searches the project for assets that match specific criteria. Params: folder_path, name, asset_type?, recursive?, tags?

epic_find_similar.summary: [Epic SemanticSearchToolset.SemanticSearchToolset] Find assets whose embeddings are semantically similar to the given asset's embedding. Vector-only (no BM25). The source asset must already be indexed by the SemanticSearch plugin. Params: assetPath, classFilter, pathRegexes, k?

epic_generate_convex_collisions.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Generates convex hull collision shapes for a static mesh. Convex hulls provide accurate collision for physics simulation. More hulls improve accuracy but increase runtime cost. Replaces any existing collision. Params: mesh, hull_count?, max_hull_verts?, hull_precision?

epic_generate_lods.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Auto-generates LODs for a static mesh using triangle reduction. Each entry in triangle_percents creates one additional LOD. The value is the fraction of triangles to keep relative to LOD 0, from just above 0.0 (nearly empty) to 1.0 (full detail). For example, [0.5, 0.25] creates LOD1 with 50% of the original triangles and LOD2 with 25%. Params: mesh, triangle_percents

epic_get_asset_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the class of an asset. Params: asset_path

epic_get_asset_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the asset registry tags for an asset. Params: asset_path

epic_get_bounds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the local-space bounding box of a static mesh. Params: mesh

epic_get_dependencies.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists assets that the specified asset depends on. Params: asset_path

epic_get_entry.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the source string for a specific key. Params: string_table, key

epic_get_items.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns cached item data. Items must be loaded in the registry cache to be returned. Params: registryName, itemNames

epic_get_keys.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Returns all keys for a row. Params: curve_table, row_name

epic_get_lod_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of LODs in a static mesh asset. Params: mesh

epic_get_lod_thresholds.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the screen-size thresholds at which each LOD becomes active. Screen size is a ratio of the mesh's screen height to the viewport height. A value of 1.0 means the mesh fills the full viewport height; values above 1.0 are valid and mean the mesh must appear larger than the viewport before the next LOD activates. Each LOD activates when the mesh appears smaller than its threshold. Params: mesh

epic_get_material.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the material assigned to a named slot on a static mesh. Params: mesh, slot_name

epic_get_material_slots.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the names of all material slots in a static mesh. Material slot names are used when assigning materials to specific parts of the mesh. Use these names with get_material and set_material. Params: mesh

epic_get_metadata_tags.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Gets the metadata tags for an asset. Params: asset_path

epic_get_namespace.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the namespace of a StringTable asset. Params: string_table

epic_get_plugin_content_paths.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Returns the root content paths for plugins that have content. Params: include_engine?

epic_get_referencers.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists assets that reference the specified asset. Params: asset_path

epic_get_registry_info.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns detailed information about a specific registry. Params: registryName

epic_get_rows.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Returns the column values for one or more rows as a JSON string. Params: data_table, row_names

epic_get_schema.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the item struct schema as JSON. Params: registryName

epic_get_schema__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Returns the column schema of the data table as a JSON string. Params: data_table

epic_get_size.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools] Returns the dimensions of a Texture2D in pixels. Params: texture

epic_get_table_id.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Returns the table ID for a StringTable asset. The table ID is derived from the asset's package path and is used to reference the string table in text properties and localisation. Params: string_table

epic_get_triangle_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of triangles in a specific LOD of a static mesh. Params: mesh, lod_index?

epic_get_vertex_count.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns the number of vertices in a specific LOD of a static mesh. Params: mesh, lod_index?

epic_import_file.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.curve_table.CurveTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a CurveTable asset. The file's first column is the row name; subsequent columns are sample times and values. interp_mode controls how the imported keys are interpolated between samples. Params: folder_path, asset_name, source_file, interp_mode

epic_import_file__data_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.data_table.DataTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a DataTable asset. The file's columns must match the property names in schema. Use search_row_structs to discover usable schema structs. Params: folder_path, asset_name, source_file, schema

epic_import_file__static_mesh_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Imports a mesh file from disk as a StaticMesh asset. Params: folder_path, asset_name, source_file, import_materials?, import_textures?, combine_meshes?

epic_import_file__string_table_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.string_table.StringTableTools] Imports a file from disk as a StringTable asset. The file must have a header row with at least 'Key' and 'SourceString' columns. Additional meta-data columns are imported but the namespace is not - the StringTable's namespace is derived from its asset path. Params: folder_path, asset_name, source_file

epic_import_file__texture_tools.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.texture.TextureTools] Imports an image file from disk as a Texture2D asset. Params: folder_path, asset_name, source_file

epic_is_checked_out.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Checks whether an asset is checked out by the current user. Params: asset_path

epic_is_dirty.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Checks whether an asset has unsaved changes. Params: asset_path

epic_is_nanite_enabled.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.static_mesh.StaticMeshTools] Returns whether Nanite is enabled for a static mesh. Nanite is Unreal's virtualized geometry system that renders highly detailed meshes efficiently. It is most beneficial for meshes with many triangles. Params: mesh

epic_list_data_sources.summary: [Epic DataRegistryToolset.DataRegistryTools] Returns the editor-defined sources configured on a Data Registry. These are the sources as authored on the registry asset, before any runtime expansion of meta sources. Params: registryName

epic_list_folders.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.asset.AssetTools] Lists the folders contained within a folder. Params: root_path, recursive?

spawn_ambient(soundPath|assetPath|path, location?:v, label?, onConflict?, volumeMultiplier|volume?:n)
metasound_author(name, packagePath?, onConflict?, format?, oneShot?:b, inputs?:[o], outputs?:[o], nodes?:[o], connections?:[o])
