action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

list_graphs.summary: List PCG graphs, sorted by object path. Lists the whole project; page through it with cursor/limit.

read_graph.summary: Read graph structure: every node with its name, title, inputPins and outputPins (the pin labels connect_nodes takes), the graph's inputNode and outputNode, and edges.

read_node_settings.summary: Read node settings. An instanced subobject (a spawner's MeshSelectorParameters or InstanceDataPackerParameters) is expanded under instanced {class, properties}, and a weighted mesh selector also lists meshEntries [{mesh, weight, materialOverrides}] (#1303).

get_component_details.summary: Inspect PCG component (#983). Reports blueprintOwned with a warning when the Blueprint's construction script builds the component (edits on the placed actor can be lost on reconstruction; use set_component_parameters with blueprintPath), isGenerating, isCleaningUp, generated, partitioned (with local component counts) and lastRun {id, state generating|generated|cancelled|cleaned|not_started, startedUtc, finishedUtc}; to wait for a run, use wait_for_generation or wait=true on execute.

create_graph.summary: Create graph in packagePath (or path), default /Game/PCG. Idempotent by path: an existing graph is reported rather than replaced.

add_node.summary: Add node. The engine assigns its name unless name is given; either way nodeName in the result is what connect_nodes and remove_node take. A name already in the graph with the same class is reported as existed; another class is refused (#1331).

connect_nodes.summary: Wire nodes. Returns edgeVerified=true after confirming the UPCGEdge persisted; surfaces an error if AddEdge succeeded but no edge object was instantiated (#304). A pin label the node does not have is refused with reason pin_not_found and validPins, the labels it does have.

disconnect_nodes.summary: Remove a wired edge between two PCG nodes. Omitted pins match any pin; a pin label the node does not have is refused with validPins. Returns removedEdges count (#346).

set_node_settings.summary: Set node params. Pass a settings object of {propertyPath: value} (dotted paths and nested structs supported), or propertyName + propertyValue for a single write. Reports previousProperties and rolls back to them. Writing a spawner's MeshSelectorType or InstanceDataPackerType recreates its selector or packer (listed in recreatedInstancedParameters). Fields of an instanced subobject the node owns are written with a dotted key (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName) or a field object ({MeshSelectorParameters: {AttributeName: 'Mesh'}}), in the same call as the type that selects its class; a path for an instanced subobject, or a dotted key into an object the node does not own, is refused. Addresses the graph's DefaultInputNode and DefaultOutputNode too: writing their Pins changes the graph's own pins and those of every Subgraph node calling it. An attribute selector (TargetAttribute, InputSource1, OutputTarget...) takes the PCG editor's syntax as a string: MyAttr, $Density, @Last, $Position.Z (#1275); a selector given as an object replaces the whole selector, so fields left out (ExtraNames) reset. Returns resolvedSelectors with each written selector as stored, and removedEdges for edges a pin-changing write dropped, with a warning (#1298). readBack holds each written property as stored; struct text that left fields out (which keep their old values) adds a warning naming the property (#1299).

set_static_mesh_spawner_meshes.summary: Populate weighted MeshEntries on a PCGStaticMeshSpawner node (#145). entries=[{mesh, weight?}]; replace defaults to true. Refuses a selector the node's settings do not own; reports selectorOuterIsSettings.

remove_node.summary: Remove node. The graph's input and output nodes are refused.

unwrap_instance_nodes.summary: Give instance nodes (UPCGSettingsInstance wrappers, read-only in the PCG editor's details panel) their own settings object, keeping every value and edge. Settings from a shared asset are copied into the node. Nodes that already own their settings are left alone. Omit nodeName for every node in the graph (#1087).

execute.summary: Regenerate PCG. A seed is written to the component before generating, and the old one reported back as previousSeed (#983). Returns at once with runId, or with wait=true only once that run finishes, adding wait {state generated|cancelled|cleaned|not_started|timed_out, durationMs}; a timed-out wait is a warning, not a failure (#1365). When Generate defers its start to a later tick, the run follows that generation (lastRun.deferredStart) instead of settling as not_started; a run that started nothing reports alreadyGenerated, lastFinishUtc and a note saying the output was already up to date. Refused with generation_in_progress while a run is active.

force_regenerate.summary: Force a stuck PCG component to regenerate (clears graph ref, re-sets, cleanup+generate) (#146/#983). Cancels active generation before resetting; returns runId like execute, including when the component was busy, and takes wait=true the same way (#1365).

get_generation_state.summary: One poll of a PCG component's generation: busy (generating, cleaning up, or local components generating), finishCount and lastFinishState for generations that ended since the bridge started watching the component (whoever started them), and lastRun. wait_for_generation polls this for you (#1365).

cleanup.summary: Cleanup a PCG component (remove spawned content) (#146).

toggle_graph.summary: Toggle a PCG component's graph assignment to force reinit (no generate) (#146).

add_volume.summary: Place PCG volume. Idempotent by editor label when one is given. transform {location, rotation, scale|scale3D} is honoured; reports the placed location, rotation, scale, extent and scaledExtent.

import_graph.summary: Bulk-author a PCG graph from JSON: nodes=[{name,class,posX?,posY?,settings?,subgraph?:{path,parameters}}], connections=[{from,fromPin?,to,toPin?}], replace defaults to false. Without replace, a name the graph already has is that node: the same class updates it in place (counted in nodesUpdated and listed in updatedNodes) and edges naming it land on it; another class, or a name given twice, refuses the call before anything changes (#1262). removeNodes and removeConnections run first, without replace. The rollback of an import without replace removes the nodes it created, cuts the edges it added and restores the values it overwrote; only replace=true carries a full graph snapshot (#1331). One call replaces N add_node + M connect_nodes + K set_node_settings (#213). A path for an instanced subobject is refused before anything changes, while its fields are written as set_node_settings writes them (MeshSelectorParameters.AttributeName or a field object); failed nodes, settings or connections make the result a failure; name-collision warnings are informational. Attribute selectors in settings take the PCG editor's syntax as a string ($Position.Z, @Last). A Get Graph Parameter node (PCGUserParameterGetSettings) takes parameter: '<name>' and binds to that graph parameter; export_graph emits it the same way (#1264).

export_graph.summary: Export a PCG graph as JSON; includeSettings defaults to true. Each node carries inputPins and outputPins, its pin labels; import_graph ignores them. Round-trip safe with import_graph (#213). Subgraph assignments and parameter overrides are preserved as subgraph {path,parameters}; other instanced subobjects (a spawner's mesh selector) are left out and listed in omittedInstancedProperties. Attribute selectors export in editor syntax ("$Position.Z"), extra names included (#1267).

export_level_to_asset.summary: Export a saved level to a PCG data asset (a PCG Assembly), the Content Browser's 'Create PCG Assets from Level(s)' without its dialog. Default name <LevelName>_PCG beside the level; an existing asset is overwritten. assetPath takes the asset's own path (object path, or an existing asset's package path) as well as a folder for assetName, and an existing asset of another class is refused (#1296). Reports points per output pin (Root, Points). UE 5.5+ (#1244).

update_level_assets.summary: Re-export PCG data assets from the levels they were exported from ('Update PCG Assets'). Reports points per output pin. UE 5.5+ (#1244).

set_subgraph.summary: Point a Subgraph node at a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance through the engine's SetSubgraph, so its pins and user-parameter bag are built (a write to SubgraphInstance.Graph builds pins but no parameters). "" clears it. Returns the node's pins and every parameter with its value and override state (#1253).

set_subgraph_parameters.summary: Override a Subgraph node's user parameters: parameters={name: value}; null clears an override. A name the subgraph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1253).

set_graph_pins.summary: Add, update, replace or remove the graph's own pins on its input or output node (side), matched by label: append (default) adds a pin or updates the one with that label, replace makes the pins exactly the list, remove deletes the labels given. Fields left out keep an existing pin's values, so its edges stay wired. Every Subgraph node calling the graph gets the same pins. Returns the resulting pins and removedEdges for edges a removed or retyped pin dropped. Rolls back to the previous Pins through set_node_settings (#1318).

set_graph_parameters.summary: Add, change, retype or remove a graph's user parameters (the Graph Parameters a Get Graph Parameter node and a Subgraph or Graph Instance override read). graphParameters=[{name, type?, typeObject?, default?}]: a new name needs a type; an existing one keeps its type unless another is given; default is JSON or export text. removeParameters=[names]. Every entry is checked on a scratch copy first, so one bad entry refuses the call with nothing changed. Returns the parameters and previousParameters; the rollback removes what was added and restores changed defaults (#1264).

create_graph_instance.summary: Create a PCG Graph Instance asset running graphPath, with optional parameter overrides={name: value}; an override for a name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, sets none and fails with the asset path in createdWithoutOverrides. Idempotent by path. Returns every parameter with its value and override state (#1264).

set_graph_instance_overrides.summary: Set a PCG Graph Instance asset's parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}; null clears one. A name the graph does not declare, or a value of the wrong type, refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and rolls back to them (#1264).

set_component_graph.summary: Assign a PCG graph to a PCGComponent through UPCGComponent::SetGraph, on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath; compiled and saved, so every placed instance rebuilds with it) or on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath). graphPath is a PCGGraph or PCGGraphInstance; "" clears it. componentName picks one when there are several. On a placed actor whose Blueprint's construction script builds the component, the call reruns the construction script and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction if the assignment did not survive. Returns graph, previousGraph and the new graph's parameters with their override state; rolls back to the previous graph (lossy when the component held overrides).

get_component_parameters.summary: Read a PCG component's graph and each graph parameter's value and override state ({name, type, value, overridden}), on a placed actor (actorLabel or actorPath) or on a Blueprint's component template (blueprintPath). componentName picks one when there are several. A placed actor's component that its Blueprint's construction script builds reports blueprintOwned and a warning: values written to the placed actor can be discarded on reconstruction, so write them to the Blueprint.

set_component_parameters.summary: Set a PCG component's graph parameter overrides: overrides={name: value}, null clears one. With blueprintPath it writes the Blueprint's component template (a child Blueprint gets its own override of an inherited one), compiles and saves, so every reconstruction keeps the overrides; this is the write for a PCGComponent inside a Blueprint actor. With actorLabel or actorPath it writes the placed component; when the Blueprint's construction script builds that component, the call reruns the construction script as the editor does and fails with reason discarded_by_reconstruction, naming the lost overrides and the Blueprint write to use, if they did not survive (persistedThroughReconstruction). A name the graph does not declare or a value of the wrong type refuses the whole call with nothing changed. Returns previous values and every parameter's value and override state, and rolls back to the previous values.

read_generated_output.summary: Read the data a PCG component generated, for any actor's PCG components (not only PCGVolumes): per tagged data its pin, tags, dataClass, kind (points | attributeSet | other), count, and a page of entries with the requested attributes (selectors such as $Position, $Density, $Position.Z or a metadata attribute; default the point properties plus every metadata attribute). offset/limit page the entries, and nextOffset says there are more. A partitioned component's local components are read too. Each component row also lists what the graph spawned, which a spawner does not hand to the output node: spawnedComponents [{name, class, owner, mesh, instanceCount}], spawnedInstanceCount and spawnedActors, with totals spawnedComponentCount and spawnedInstanceCount on the result. With nodeName it reads that node's output from the component's inspection instead (UE 5.8+): the first call turns inspection on and asks for a regenerate, later calls return each execution stack's data (#1309).

epic_add_comment_box.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a comment box around the given nodes. Params: graph, nodes, comment?, color?

epic_add_node.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a native node to the graph. Params: graph, nativeNodeType, nodeName, jsonParams, nodeTitle, nodeComment, xPositionIdx?, yPositionIdx?

epic_add_subgraph_node.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Adds a subgraph node to the graph. Params: graph, subGraphForNode, nodeName, jsonParams, nodeTitle, nodeComment, xPositionIdx?, yPositionIdx?

epic_connect_node_pins.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Add an edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins. Params: fromNode, fromPinLabel, toNode, toPinLabel

epic_create_graph.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Creates a new saved PCG graph asset. Params: name, path?

epic_disconnect_node_pins.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Removes the edge between two nodes connected to the specified pins. Params: fromNode, fromPinLabel, toNode, toPinLabel

epic_draw_spline.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Triggers the user to draw a spline in the viewport to be used later in the world building. Waits for the user to be done. Params: actorLabel, actorTag, bRedraw, bClosedSpline

epic_execute_graph_instance.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Executes the graph instance and returns any issues encountered during execution. Params: pCGVolume

epic_get_graph_description.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns the description of a PCG graph. Params: graph

epic_get_graph_instance_params.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Gets the graph instance params of a specific actor, actor MUST have a graph instance Params: pCGVolume

epic_get_graph_schema.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns the schema for a PCG Graph's graph parameters Params: graph

epic_get_graph_structure.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns the complete structure of a PCG graph including all nodes, connections, exposed parameters, and comment boxes. Params: graph

epic_get_native_node_schema.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns the schema for a PCG node type including input/output pins, parameters, and their types. Params: nodeName

epic_get_node_data_view.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns a JSON Data View of a specific node's output data from the last graph execution. On first call, enables inspection so future ExecuteGraphInstance calls store per-node data. If no inspection data exists, returns an error prompting re-execution. IMPORTANT: Inspection state is shared at the graph asset level. If multiple actors use the same graph, you MUST call this tool (and ExecuteGraphInstance) on only one actor at a time. Wait for each call to fully complete before calling on the next actor. Concurrent calls on actors sharing the same graph will cause a freeze. Params: pCGVolume, node, pinLabel?, attributeName, startIndex?, endIndex?

epic_get_node_info.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns node details including name, position, and all parameter values. Params: node

epic_list_available_subgraphs.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Lists the PCG graphs that can be used with the Subgraph native node. Only these graphs should be used with the Subgraph native node. Params: none

epic_list_graph_instances.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Gets all actors with a PCG graph instance in the scene. Params: none

epic_list_native_nodes.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Returns a list of available native PCG node type names. Params: bCommonOnly?

epic_remove_comment_box.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Removes a comment box from the graph. Does not affect the nodes it contains. Params: graph, commentId

epic_remove_graph_params.summary: [Epic PCGToolset.PCGToolset] Removes graph parameters to a specific PCG graph, such that they are not overridable anymore. Params: graph, paramNames

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

inject_input.summary: Inject one frame of an Enhanced Input action into a PIE player. client 1..N relays to a remote player.

inject_input_start.summary: Start holding an input action; returns injection_id. Rolls back with inject_input_stop.

inject_input_update.summary: Change the value of a running hold.

inject_input_stop.summary: Stop a hold or tape by id; alreadyStopped when it had ended.

inject_input_tape.summary: Play a per-frame value array through an input action; returns injection_id.

clients.summary: List a networked PIE session's players: client 0 is the editor's own player, 1..N remote players in join order with ready and log_file.

console.summary: Run a console command in a remote player's own process (client 1..N). The editor's own PIE player is editor(execute_command, world="pie").

remote_result.summary: Whether a request relayed to a remote player ran: reported, ok, finished, error.

uat_run.summary: Run a multiplayer acceptance scenario unattended: opens its map, starts PIE with its players, drives each step, judges it from the host and client logs, stops PIE and writes report.md and report.json. Poll uat_status.

uat_status.summary: State of the current or last acceptance run: per-step results, verdict and report_dir.

uat_abort.summary: End the acceptance run early; it stops PIE and reports what it reached.

record_arm.summary: Arm the PIE recorder; it starts on BeginPIE and finalizes on EndPIE into Saved/MCPRecordings/<id>. Rolls back with record_disarm.

record_status.summary: Recorder state, id, frame and elapsed time.

record_read.summary: Read a recording artifact: manifest, sequence, csv, drift or tracked.

mark.summary: Insert a labelled marker into the recording in flight.

replay_arm.summary: Arm the replayer for the next PIE session: re-injects a recording's input and records drift. Rolls back with replay_disarm.

replay_run.summary: Unattended replay: arm and start PIE in one call, auto-stop PIE and write drift.json. Poll replay_status until pie_active=false.

replay_status.summary: Replayer state and the last result: drift report, frames and contact sheet paths.

replay_analyze.summary: Read a finalized drift.json as a lead: first divergence, top channels, errors during the run, bracketing images.

replay_state.summary: Deterministic state replay: the recorded pawn pose at a time or frame, interpolated; apply=true teleports the live PIE pawn there.

test_scaffold.summary: Write a reproduction test.json beside a recording: drift and error assertions plus derived predicates.

test_run.summary: Run a reproduction test: replay the recording when needed, then check drift, errors and predicates. Returns passed and failures.

assert_eval.summary: Evaluate predicates over a finished run's per-frame series, errors and markers; writes verdict.json. Ops eq|ne|lt|lte|gt|gte|approx|between|changed|increased|decreased|crossed under hold always|never|eventually|at_end|once_then_always.

record_diff.summary: Diff two recordings frame by frame against drift thresholds.

scenario_scaffold.summary: Write a declarative scenario.json (arrange, act, assert) from a recording.

scenario_validate.summary: Validate a scenario's structure and predicates without running it.

profile_create.summary: Create an observation profile asset: tracked values, actors and widgets, pawn and montage sampling, drift thresholds.

profile_update.summary: Update an observation profile; lists given replace the stored ones.

observe_arm.summary: Arm the observer with a profile; it samples every frame of the next PIE session into Saved/MCPObservations/<run>. Rolls back with observe_disarm.

observe_read.summary: Read an observation artifact; file=series returns per-channel time series.

anim_state.summary: A PIE actor's anim instance: active montage and state machine states.

anim_properties.summary: UPROPERTY values on a PIE actor's anim instance.

session_errors.summary: Deduped errors and warnings logged during a PIE session, with Blueprint exceptions.

session_log.summary: Paged Output Log lines captured during a PIE session, with filters.

perf_summary.summary: A recording's frametime avg/p50/p99/max, game/render/gpu ms, peak memory and worst hitches.

script_create.summary: Create a test script asset: steps of {instruction, judge auto|manual, arrange, act, expect {value, op decreasing|increasing|eq|gt|lt|visible|exists, target, within_ms}}. arrange takes a scenario's spawn|set|call entries and act takes uat_run's step actions (place, press, inject, hold, tape, console, capture, wait_ms); they run in that order before the expect window, which counts from the end of act. Always saves, returning what the check finds as warnings [{step, field, message, candidates}]: an expect.value the level, player pawn and profile do not resolve, an op or target the value's type cannot meet, an actor, actor class or Input Action arrange and act name that does not exist, or no auto step without manual_only=true. resolve_in_pie=true on a step defers a value that only exists in PIE. Refused (INVALID_SCRIPT_STEPS, errors in the same shape) only when the script cannot be written: no steps, a step that does not parse, or a map (e.g. /Game/Maps/L_Arena) that is not a level.

script_update.summary: Update a test script; steps given replace the stored ones. Checks the result like script_create when steps, profile, map or manual_only change, and saves with its findings as warnings; refuses only what cannot be written.

script_validate.summary: Check steps the way script_create does without saving anything: valid, and errors [{step, field, message, candidates}] for every finding script_create would return as a warning or refuse.

script_values.summary: What a script can name in the open level: the player pawn's readable value paths with kind and type, level actors, classes the game mode spawns, Widget Blueprints and the profile's tracked values. target adds which actors are of that class and whether it is the player pawn.

script_list.summary: List test scripts, each with map and last_run: its newest run's run_id, state, started_at, ended_at, summary and results_path, or null.

script_run.summary: Run a test script in PIE: opens the script's map first when another level is open, refusing when that level has unsaved changes or PIE is running elsewhere; arms the observer and, unless record=false, the recorder; mode=manual instead starts no PIE, observer or recording, leaves auto steps unchecked and puts every manual step up for its verdict at once; evaluates auto steps live and marks each pass or fail; waits on manual steps for verdicts, asked through an elicitation form when the client supports one, otherwise through verdict. Writes results.json beside the observation. wait=true returns once the run finishes.

script_status.summary: A script run's state, steps and events since since_seq. wait=true blocks until it finishes or needs a verdict.

script_stop.summary: End a script run now; unsettled steps stay pending and results.json is written.

verdict.summary: Record a manual step's verdict: pass, fail or skip, with a note. source=agent marks the calling agent's own judgement and needs evidence {note, captures?}; a step with agent_judgeable=false takes only a person's verdict.

script_runs.summary: List script runs newest first, the active one included: run_id, script, started_at, ended_at, state, summary, per-step results and results_path. script narrows to one script's runs.

script_replay.summary: Replay a finished run's recording in the level it ran in and re-evaluate its auto steps at their recorded offsets; manual steps keep their verdicts. Reports regressions.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

generate_project_files.summary: Generate IDE project files (Visual Studio, Xcode, etc.).

create_cpp_class.summary: Create a new native UCLASS in a project module. Uses the same engine template path as File → New C++ Class. Writes .h + .cpp; returns both paths plus needsEditorRestart (true unless Live Coding successfully hot-reloaded).

list_project_modules.summary: List native modules in the current project (name, host type, source path), in the .uproject's own declaration order. Feed moduleName from here into create_cpp_class.

list_available_plugins.summary: List every plugin installed in this engine or project, sorted by name, with its category, version, type, whether it is enabled in THIS editor session, whether it is enabled by default, and the .uproject's current reference to it under projectReference {present, enabled}. Those two disagree after enable_plugin until the editor restarts, which is the point of reporting both.

enable_plugin.summary: Enable a plugin in the .uproject. Plugin enablement is neither a UPROPERTY nor an INI key, it is a JSON array in the .uproject read once at startup, so set_config cannot reach it and without this a plugin-gated capability stays permanently unreachable through the bridge. Idempotent: a plugin already enabled, or enabled by default with no entry, reports existed and writes nothing. The change is a file change, so modules, classes, content and settings appear only after editor(restart_editor), which the result says. Only the plugin's entry in the on-disk .uproject Plugins array is patched; every other field, including a Modules edit made while the editor runs, is left as the file has it (#1248).

disable_plugin.summary: Disable a plugin in the .uproject. removeReference deletes the entry outright instead of writing an explicit disable, which is the difference between handing a default-on plugin back to its default and overriding it, and the two are not the same file. Idempotent against whichever of the two was asked for. Refuses to disable the bridge itself, since that would leave no way to undo it. Patches only that entry of the on-disk .uproject (#1248). Takes effect on the next editor start.

live_coding_compile.summary: Trigger a Live Coding compile (Windows only). Hot-patches method bodies of existing UCLASSes without editor restart - the fast inner loop for UFUNCTION implementations. Does NOT reliably register brand-new UCLASSes; use build_project + editor restart for those.

live_coding_status.summary: Report Live Coding availability/state (available, started, enabledForSession, compiling). Helps choose between live_coding_compile and build_project.

resolve_collision_profile.summary: Read one collision profile's resolved per-channel responses: collisionEnabled, objectType, and every channel with Block/Overlap/Ignore. This is the project-side half of blueprint(get_component_collision) (#925): a component's ResponseArray only lists the channels it OVERRIDES, so the profile is where an inherited response actually comes from. Project trace and object channels appear under their configured names, with enumName (ECC_GameTraceChannel1) alongside so a caller can key on something stable. By default the eight engine channels plus every channel the project configured are returned; includeAllChannels=true adds the unused slots. channel narrows it to one. A profile that does not exist lists the ones that do.

epic_discover_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Initialize automation worker discovery and load the test list. Must be called once before ListTests or RunTests. Takes several seconds as it discovers the local automation worker and enumerates all registered tests. Returns an async result that completes with a JSON status object when tests are available, or an error if discovery fails. Params: bForceRediscover?

epic_get_section_property_values.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns the current values of the specified properties as a JSON object. Raises an error if the section does not exist, has no settings object, or any requested property cannot be read. Params: containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertyNames

epic_get_section_schema.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Returns a JSON Schema describing the user-visible properties of a settings section. The schema maps each property name to its type, description, and constraints. Raises an error if the section does not exist or has no backing settings object (e.g. uses a custom widget instead). Params: containerName, categoryName, sectionName

epic_get_test_results.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get detailed results for the current or most recent test run. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Returns a JSON object with per-test state, duration, errors, and warnings. Params: none

epic_get_test_status.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Get a lightweight status snapshot of the automation controller. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Returns a JSON object with the controller state, enabled test count, and completion/pass/fail counts. Params: none

epic_list_categories.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all categories within a settings container, sorted alphabetically. Raises an error if the container does not exist. Params: containerName

epic_list_containers.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all known settings containers, sorted alphabetically. Common containers are "Editor" and "Project". Params: none

epic_list_sections.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Lists the names of all sections within a settings category, sorted alphabetically. Raises an error if the container or category does not exist. Params: containerName, categoryName

epic_list_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] List available automation tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Returns a JSON object: {"tests": ["path1", ...], "total": N, "returned": N}. Params: nameFilter, tagFilter, limit?

epic_reset_section_to_defaults.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Resets the settings in a section to their default values. Raises an error if the section does not exist or reset is not supported. Params: containerName, categoryName, sectionName

epic_run_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run a set of automation tests by name. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Starts executing the specified tests and returns an async result that completes with a JSON summary when all tests finish. Params: testNames

epic_run_tests_by_filter.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Run automation tests selected by a filter expression. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. Much faster than RunTests when targeting a large batch because the engine narrows the report tree in a single pass instead of running a per-leaf membership check against the requested name list. Filter syntax (multiple expressions joined by '+'): "StartsWith:System.Engine" prefix match against the full test path "^Foo" prefix anchor (equivalent to StartsWith:) "Bar$" suffix anchor "Substring" bare token matches anywhere in the path "Group:Smoke" expand a named group from AutomationControllerSettings ini Groups Returns an async result that completes with the same JSON summary as RunTests. Params: filterExpression

epic_save_section.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Saves the settings in a section. Raises an error if the section does not exist or saving is not supported. Params: containerName, categoryName, sectionName

epic_set_section_properties.summary: [Epic ConfigSettingsToolset.ConfigSettingsToolset] Sets one or more properties on a settings section from a JSON object and saves. PropertiesJson must be a JSON object mapping property names to new values, in the same format returned by GetSectionPropertyValues. Raises an error if the section does not exist, cannot be edited, has no settings object, the default config file is not writable, or any property cannot be set. Params: containerName, categoryName, sectionName, propertiesJson

epic_stop_tests.summary: [Epic AutomationTestToolset.AutomationTestToolset] Stop all currently running tests. Requires DiscoverTests() to have completed. If a RunTests async result is pending, it will be completed with an error. Params: none

tools.name: reflection
tools.description:
UE reflection: classes, structs, enums, gameplay tags, and SaveGame instances.

Call reflection(action, args={...}). Actions:
reflect_class(className, includeInherited?:b)
reflect_instance(objectPath, propertyPath?, filter?, includeInherited?:b, includeValues?:b, editableOnly?:b, maxDepth?:i, cursor?, limit?:i)
reflect_struct(structName)
reflect_enum(enumName)
list_classes(parentFilter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
list_structs(package?, filter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
list_tags(filter?, cursor?, limit?:i)
create_tag(tag, comment?)
create_enum(name, packagePath?, entries?:[*], onConflict?)
set_enum_entries(assetPath, entries:[*])
is_class_loaded(className|class)
is_module_loaded(moduleName|module)
list_loaded_modules(filter?, loadedOnly?:b, cursor?, limit?:i)
inspect_save_game(slotName, userIndex?:i)
epic_get_class(instance:ref)
epic_get_properties(instance:ref, properties:[s])
epic_list_properties(instance:ref)
epic_reset_properties(instance:ref, properties:[s])
epic_search_subclasses(base_class:ref, class_name)
epic_set_properties(instance:ref, values)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

reflect_class.summary: Reflect UClass properties and functions. To call a static BlueprintCallable editor function with arguments and return values, use editor(invoke_static_function) with className, functionName and args. className accepts the C++ spelling with or without the A/U/F/E prefix (UMyConfig and MyConfig both resolve), a /Script/Module.ClassName path, or a Blueprint class path; a failed lookup lists the spellings tried and the closest matches (#823).

reflect_instance.summary: Per-instance writable schema: what can be written on THIS asset, CDO or subobject right now. reflect_class answers what a class has; this answers what the object in front of you will accept, which is what removes the write-and-see loop. Per property: type and kind, the same tooltip/category/displayName/clamp/UI-range/units metadata reflect_class reports, the UPROPERTY flag names, the current value and valueText, and the constraints a write has to satisfy - enum values, allowed and disallowed classes for an object reference, array/set element type, map key and value types, struct field layout, container element count. Instance state on top of that: 'editable' with a 'notEditableReason' (EditConst, EditDefaultsOnly read on an instance, EditInstanceOnly read on defaults), the EditCondition and whether it is met on THIS object, 'settable' saying whether asset/editor(set_property) can write it at all, and 'valueObjectPath' for an instanced subobject so the next call can aim at it. objectPath takes an asset path, an object path, a class path or a Blueprint path (its generated-class defaults). propertyPath scopes the read to one nested struct or object reference, including one array element picked by key (`Profiles[ProfileId=Axe].Presentation`).

reflect_enum.summary: Reflect UEnum by full path, short name, or short name without the E prefix. Resolves native enums in any loaded module and loads unloaded Blueprint (UserDefinedEnum) assets via the asset registry. Returns enumPath, userDefined, and per-value name/value/displayName/tooltip; a failed lookup lists close matches (#762).

list_classes.summary: List classes. parentFilter resolves with or without the C++ A/U/F/E prefix (#823). Rows carry name, path and parent, sorted by path so a page boundary is stable.

list_structs.summary: List UScriptStructs, native and user-defined. Rows carry name (the registered spelling, without the F prefix), cppName (with it), path, package, parent, native and tableRow (derives from FTableRowBase, so usable as a DataTable row struct), sorted by path so a page boundary is stable. package narrows to one package or content folder: /Script/Engine, a bare module name (Engine), or /Game/Data. filter is a case-insensitive substring of name or cppName (#1088).

list_tags.summary: List gameplay tags, optionally only those under a prefix.

create_tag.summary: Create a gameplay tag in Config/DefaultGameplayTags.ini. Inserts exactly one +GameplayTagList line, keeping the file's comments, order and existing values, and rebuilds the live tag tree so the tag is usable without a restart (method=ini_append, registeredLive). Only when the file cannot be written does it fall back to the Gameplay Tags editor, which can check the file out but rewrites it whole (method=gameplay_tags_editor) (#1322). Idempotent: a tag the ini already declares reports existed. A failure names the ini path and the cause, including a read-only (checked-in) file.

create_enum.summary: Create UUserDefinedEnum asset, optionally seeded with entries: strings, or {name, displayName?} objects (#274).

set_enum_entries.summary: Replace entries on an existing UUserDefinedEnum. entries takes the create_enum form: strings, or {name, displayName?} (#274).

is_class_loaded.summary: Report whether a UClass is currently loaded in the editor (loaded), whether it exists/is loadable (exists), and its owning module + that module's load state. Distinguishes 'not loaded yet' from 'does not exist'. className takes a short name, /Script/<Module>.<Class>, or a BP class path (#689).

is_module_loaded.summary: Report whether a named module is currently loaded (#689).

list_loaded_modules.summary: Enumerate modules with runtime load state. filter is a case-insensitive substring; loadedOnly defaults to false. Returns modules[{name, loaded, gameModule}] + totalLoaded/totalModules (#689).

inspect_save_game.summary: Load a SaveGame slot read-only and return its reflected UPROPERTY(SaveGame) values. Non-serializable properties are listed in skippedProperties instead of failing the call. userIndex defaults to 0.

epic_get_class.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns the class of an Unreal object. Params: instance

epic_get_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns the values of one or more properties on an object. Params: instance, properties

epic_list_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Returns a list of properties that are on the specified object. Params: instance

epic_reset_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Resets one or more properties on an object to their default values, removing any per-instance overrides. Params: instance, properties

epic_search_subclasses.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Finds all subclasses of a given class. Params: base_class, class_name

epic_set_properties.summary: [Epic editor_toolset.toolsets.object.ObjectTools] Sets the values of properties on an object. Params: instance, values

tools.name: source_control
tools.description:
Source control through the editor's own provider (Perforce, Git, Unity Version Control, Subversion): provider, connection and supported operations, file status, history, the project's pending changes, checkout, add, mark for delete, revert, sync, diff, submit, and whether bridge writes check out read-only files automatically. Provider-specific actions (shelves, streams, branches) come from provider plugins injected here under their own prefix, such as p4_*.

Call source_control(action, args={...}). Actions:
get_provider()
get_status(paths:[s], limit?:i)
list_changes(paths?:[s], limit?:i, includeUntracked?:b)
checkout(paths:[s])
add(paths:[s])
revert(paths:[s], dryRun?:b, discardUnsaved?:b, restoreFrom?:o)
diff(path, openEditor?:b, contextLines?:i, maxLines?:i)
submit(paths:[s], description)
mark_for_delete(paths:[s])
sync(paths?:[s])
history(path, limit?:i)
connect(password?)
set_checkout_mode(mode:{manual,auto})

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

get_provider.summary: The active provider, whether it is enabled and connected, its status fields (port, user, client or workspace, branch, repository, where the provider reports them), what it supports (checkout, changelists, diff against the depot), which source_control actions the provider can run (operations, asked of the provider where the engine supports it) and the bridge's checkout mode. Call this first. With no provider configured it reports enabled=false rather than failing.

get_status.summary: State of named assets, files or folders, refreshed from the provider: checked out, added, deleted, modified, conflicted, out of date, checked out by another user (otherUser), what can be done next (canCheckout, canAdd, canRevert, canSubmit) and unsavedInEditor for a loaded package. A folder reports every file the provider knows under it, up to limit.

list_changes.summary: Every changed, added, deleted, opened or untracked file under the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders (or the paths given), with its state. Where the provider uses changelists (Perforce) each file names its changelist and changelists lists them with descriptions. Capped at limit with total and truncated; a failed refresh is reported as a warning over the cached list rather than an error.

checkout.summary: Check out (open for edit) files so they can be saved. Reports checkedOut, alreadyCheckedOut and failed with a reason per file (locked by another user, out of date, not under source control). On a provider without checkout (Git) the files are reported as checkoutNotRequired. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call checked out.

add.summary: Mark new files for add. A file must exist on disk, so save a new asset first. Reports added, alreadyControlled and failed per file. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call added.

revert.summary: Revert files to the repository revision, discarding local edits. dryRun=true lists what would be reverted (wouldRevert) and changes nothing. Unsaved editor edits to a named package are reported (unsavedInEditor) and refuse the call unless discardUnsaved=true. Loaded packages are unloaded and reloaded around the revert; a loaded map must be closed first. No inverse: the discarded edits are gone.

diff.summary: Diff one file against its latest repository revision. A text file (config, source, .uproject) returns a unified diff with addedLines and removedLines, capped at maxLines. A package returns its status and the revision it would be compared with; openEditor=true opens the editor's asset diff window against that revision.

submit.summary: Submit (Perforce, Subversion, Unity Version Control) or commit (Git) the named files with a description. Only the named files are submitted, never implicitly. Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Reports submitted and failed per file. No inverse: a submit is in the repository history, and undoing it is a new change.

mark_for_delete.summary: Mark files for delete in the repository. Where the provider removes the file from disk on delete (Git, Perforce) it is gone locally too. Reports markedForDelete, alreadyDeleted and failed per file (marked for add, not under source control, locked). Files with unsaved editor edits refuse the call; a clean loaded package is listed under loadedInEditor. Rolls back by reverting exactly the files this call marked.

sync.summary: Sync (Perforce get latest, Git pull) the named paths, or the project's Content, Config, Source and Plugins folders, to the latest repository revision. Packages under the paths with unsaved editor edits refuse the call. Loaded packages whose file changed are reloaded (reloaded); changedFiles lists the named files and loaded packages the sync rewrote. No inverse: going back is another sync.

history.summary: Revision history of one asset or file, newest first: revision, user, date, action, description, changelist (checkInIdentifier) and file size per revision, capped at limit with total and truncated.

connect.summary: Connect, or reconnect, the editor's configured provider, with an optional password or ticket for providers that log in. Reports wasConnected and connected, and the provider's own error text when it fails. The password is never echoed.

set_checkout_mode.summary: Choose what a bridge write does with a read-only file under source control for the rest of the editor session. manual (the default) refuses and names source_control(checkout); auto checks the file out first and lists it on the result as autoCheckedOut. UE_MCP_CHECKOUT_MODE=auto at editor startup turns it on from the start. Rolls back to the previous mode.

tools.name: statetree
tools.description:
StateTree asset editing: read, modify states/tasks/conditions/transitions/bindings/evaluators/global tasks/colors/state parameters/root parameters, compile and validate.

Call statetree(action, args={...}). Actions:
read(assetPath)
list_states(assetPath, cursor?, limit?:i)
add_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, name, stateType?, selectionBehavior?, insertIndex?:i, linkedSubtree?)
remove_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)
set_state_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, propertyName, value)
clear_state_nodes(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)
add_task(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o)
add_enter_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)
remove_enter_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, conditionIndex:i)
remove_task(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i)
set_task_instance_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i, propertyName, value)
set_task_property(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, taskIndex:i, propertyName, value)
add_transition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, trigger, transitionType, eventTag?, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, priority?, delayDuration?:n, bDelayTransition?:b)
add_transition_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)
remove_transition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i)
add_binding(assetPath, sourceStructId, sourcePath, targetStructId, targetPath)
remove_binding(assetPath, targetStructId, targetPath)
list_bindings(assetPath, structId?)
list_bindable_sources(assetPath, cursor?, limit?:i)
add_evaluator(assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?:o)
remove_evaluator(assetPath, nodeId)
set_evaluator_instance_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)
set_evaluator_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)
add_global_task(assetPath, structType, instanceProperties?:o)
remove_global_task(assetPath, nodeId)
set_global_task_instance_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)
set_global_task_property(assetPath, nodeId, propertyName, value)
list_colors(assetPath)
add_color(assetPath, displayName, color?)
list_state_parameters(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)
add_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, paramType)
remove_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName)
set_state_parameter(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, paramName, value)
set_root_parameters(assetPath, parameters:[o])
set_schema(assetPath, schema?)
compile(assetPath)
validate(assetPath)
list_node_types(assetPath, nodeType?, filter?, includeInstanceProperties?:b, schemaAllowedOnly?:b)
read_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?)
add_consideration(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, structType, instanceProperties?:o, operand?)
remove_consideration(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, considerationIndex:i)
remove_transition_condition(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, transitionIndex:i, conditionIndex:i)
set_state_link(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, linkType, targetStateId?, targetStatePath?, linkedAsset?)
move_state(assetPath, stateId?, statePath?, newParentStateId?, newParentStatePath?, toRoot?:b, insertIndex?:i)
set_node_class(assetPath, nodeId, nodeClass)
read_runtime(actorLabel?, actorPath?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?:i, includeDebugStrings?:b)
send_event(actorLabel?, actorPath?, eventTag, componentName?, origin?, world?, pieInstance?:i)
request_transition(actorLabel?, actorPath?, targetStateId?, targetStateTag?, priority?, fallback?, componentName?, world?, pieInstance?:i)
epic_get_children(state:ref)
epic_get_editor_data(state_tree:ref)
epic_get_enter_conditions(state:ref)
epic_get_evaluators(state_tree:ref)
epic_get_global_tasks(state_tree:ref)
epic_get_node_description(state_tree:ref, node:o)
epic_get_root_states(state_tree:ref)
epic_get_tasks(state:ref)
epic_get_transitions(state:ref)

action.description: Action to perform. One of the listed values; anything else returns the closest matches.

args.description: The action's parameters, named as its signature names them.

read.summary: Full dump of a StateTree asset: state hierarchy (with description, tag, customTickRate, color), tasks, conditions, transitions, evaluators, global tasks, root params, bindings.

list_states.summary: List all states with IDs and paths, depth-first in the tree's authored order, cursor-paginated.

add_state.summary: Add a child state under the parent named by stateId or statePath, or a root state when neither is given.

set_state_property.summary: Set a property on a state (name|type|selectionBehavior|bEnabled|weight|linkedAsset|description|tag|customTickRate|color). For tag: gameplay tag string or empty to clear. For customTickRate: number in seconds or empty to disable. For color: palette color display name, GUID, or empty to clear.

clear_state_nodes.summary: Remove all tasks/conditions/transitions from a state.

add_task.summary: Add a task to a state. structType is a C++ struct name, e.g. FMyStateTreeTask or an engine-shipped task like FStateTreeRunParallelStateTreesTask.

add_enter_condition.summary: Add an enter condition to a state.

remove_enter_condition.summary: Remove an enter condition by index.

set_task_instance_property.summary: Set a property on a task's instance data.

set_task_property.summary: Set a property on the task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level: bConsideredForCompletion, bTaskEnabled, bShouldStateChangeOnReselect). Distinct from set_task_instance_property which targets instance data. value is string-encoded, e.g. 'true'/'false'.

add_transition.summary: Add a transition to a state.

add_transition_condition.summary: Add a condition to an existing transition.

list_bindings.summary: List all property bindings, optionally filtered to one struct.

list_bindable_sources.summary: Enumerate the context/bindable sources in a StateTree (context objects, parameters, evaluators, global tasks, per-state nodes) with their structId + struct type - what a property can bind FROM, sorted by structId, cursor-paginated (#681).

add_evaluator.summary: Add an evaluator to the StateTree (tree-level).

remove_evaluator.summary: Remove an evaluator by node ID.

set_evaluator_instance_property.summary: Set a property on an evaluator's instance data.

set_evaluator_property.summary: Set a property on the evaluator's node struct (FStateTreeEvaluatorBase-level).

add_global_task.summary: Add a global task to the StateTree (tree-level).

remove_global_task.summary: Remove a global task by node ID.

set_global_task_instance_property.summary: Set a property on a global task's instance data.

set_global_task_property.summary: Set a property on a global task's node struct (FStateTreeTaskBase-level).

list_colors.summary: List all color palette entries for a StateTree. Returns: colors[] with id, displayName, color.

add_color.summary: Add a new color to the StateTree palette.

list_state_parameters.summary: List parameters defined on a state. Returns: parameters[] with name, id, type, value; also bFixedLayout.

add_state_parameter.summary: Add a parameter to a state's property bag. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states.

remove_state_parameter.summary: Remove a parameter from a state's property bag by name. Rejects fixed-layout (linked) states.

set_state_parameter.summary: Set the value of an existing state parameter. On fixed-layout states, also marks the parameter as overridden.

set_schema.summary: Attach or replace the StateTree schema, then compile. The schema is what makes a tree compilable: without one the compiler logs "does not have a schema" and stops, and everything that loads the asset reports it as failed to link. Repairs a tree that has no editor data at all (what asset(create_asset_by_class) writes) by creating the editor data, the schema and a root state. Omit schema to take StateTreeComponentSchema, then StateTreeAIComponentSchema, then whatever concrete schema this editor has, and read schemaSource / schemaNote to see which was used (#833).

compile.summary: Compile a StateTree asset. Returns success, errors[], warnings[].

validate.summary: Validate a StateTree asset without compiling.

list_node_types.summary: Enumerate every task, condition, evaluator and utility consideration THIS tree's schema allows, with the exact structType string add_task / add_enter_condition / add_transition_condition / add_consideration / add_evaluator / add_global_task take, and the property names their instanceProperties map accepts. Every add_* action takes a C++ struct name and nothing listed them, so authoring meant guessing. Also reports the schema's own capability flags (allowEnterConditions, allowUtilityConsiderations, allowEvaluators, allowMultipleTasks, allowGlobalParameters), which is what decides whether an add would be refused, and the context data a binding can come from. Blueprint-authored nodes are listed separately with the wrapper struct and the two calls that author one, because a Blueprint node needs set_node_class after the wrapper is added.

read_state.summary: Read ONE state whole, including everything the tree-wide read omits: utility considerations, the LinkedSubtree link, RequiredEventToEnter, TasksCompletion, Weight, and every transition's priority, enabled flag, delay variance and reactivation rule. Returns the state's objectPath, which is how the fields with no typed setter are written - editor(set_property) at that path reaches Transitions[0].Priority and the rest. problems[] names the faults a state cannot report about itself: utility selection with no scoring considerations anywhere below it, considerations whose parent never reads them, a Linked type pointing at nothing, and a transition targeting a deleted state. Pass stateId OR statePath.

add_consideration.summary: Add a utility consideration to a state, which is what produces the score a parent uses when its selectionBehavior is TrySelectChildrenWithHighestUtility or TrySelectChildrenAtRandomWeightedByUtility. Those behaviours were already settable and nothing could add the scoring half, so the setting could be written and never did anything. Refuses when the tree's schema does not allow considerations, and warns when the PARENT does not select by utility, because that is the silent failure. Pass stateId OR statePath.

remove_consideration.summary: Remove a utility consideration from a state by index. The rollback captures the struct type, operand and instance values, and says plainly that a replay appends at the end with a new nodeId rather than restoring its position or its bindings. Pass stateId OR statePath.

remove_transition_condition.summary: Remove one condition from a transition by index. add_transition_condition shipped without it, so a mistyped condition could only be undone by deleting the whole transition. Pass stateId OR statePath.

set_state_link.summary: Link a state to a Subtree state in THIS asset, or to another StateTree asset, or clear both. UStateTreeState carries two separate link fields and only the asset one had any route: add_state documented a linkedSubtree parameter and assigned LinkedAsset with it, so in-asset subtree reuse was impossible. Goes through SetLinkedState / SetLinkedStateAsset rather than assigning the field, which is what pulls the linked target's parameters into this state - without that a linked state has an empty fixed-layout parameter list and set_state_parameter has nothing to override. Pass stateId OR statePath; for linkType subtree pass targetStateId OR targetStatePath, for asset pass linkedAsset.

move_state.summary: Reparent or reorder an existing state. add_state takes an insertIndex for a NEW state and nothing could move one afterwards, so wrong order meant delete and rebuild - and order is load-bearing, since TrySelectChildrenInOrder walks it and NextState and NextSelectableState transitions resolve through it. Refuses to move a state under its own descendant, which would detach the branch. insertIndex is the final position among siblings; omit it to append. Reports unchanged when the state is already there, and rolls back to its previous parent and index. Pass stateId OR statePath, and newParentStateId OR newParentStatePath OR toRoot.

set_node_class.summary: Point a Blueprint node wrapper at its Blueprint class AND reallocate its instance data. This is the step with no property-write equivalent: the wrapper reports the Blueprint class AS its instance data type, so a node added before the class is set has no instance data at all, and writing the class afterwards does not go back and allocate it. Works on any task, condition, transition condition, consideration, evaluator or global task, addressed by the nodeId every add_* action returns. Returns instanceObjectPath, where the Blueprint's own variables live for editor(set_property).

read_runtime.summary: Read a RUNNING StateTree in depth: run status, last tick status, the state change count, the active states, the execution frames and the pending event queue. gameplay(get_state_tree_runtime) answers the same question with active state names only, which cannot tell you whether the tree succeeded, failed or stopped, nor whether an event you sent is still waiting to be consumed. Needs a game world, so run it in PIE. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath.

send_event.summary: Send a gameplay event to a running StateTree, which is how an event-driven tree is meant to be driven from outside and had no route at all. The event is QUEUED and consumed on the tree's next tick, so the snapshot returned still shows the state before it is handled; read it again with read_runtime after a tick. Refuses an unregistered tag, since no transition could ever match one. Has no inverse: once queued it is consumed and whatever it triggered has run. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath.

request_transition.summary: Force a running StateTree to transition to a named state, resolved through the COMPILED data - so a state added since the last compile is reported as missing rather than silently ignored. Queued like an event and resolved on the next tick against every other pending request by priority. Refuses when the tree is not Running, naming the status it is in. targetStateTag needs UE 5.8 or later; targetStateId works everywhere. Pass actorLabel OR actorPath, and targetStateId OR targetStateTag.

epic_get_children.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns child states of a state. Params: state

epic_get_editor_data.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns the editor data for a StateTree asset. Params: state_tree

epic_get_enter_conditions.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns enter conditions on a state. Params: state

epic_get_global_tasks.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns global tasks that run across all states. Params: state_tree

epic_get_node_description.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns a human-readable description for a node. Params: state_tree, node

epic_get_root_states.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns top-level states of a StateTree. Params: state_tree

epic_get_tasks.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns tasks on a state. Params: state

epic_get_transitions.summary: [Epic state_tree_toolset.toolsets.state_tree.StateTreeTools] Returns transitions on a state. Params: state

tools.name: widget

One parameter contract across every action (#798): the asset is always `assetPath`, an Unreal package path such as `/Game/UI/WBP_Example`; a widget inside the tree is always `widgetName`; its parent panel is always `parentWidgetName`; arguments for any wrapped `epic_*` action go in `input`, and a top-level `assetPath` is folded into the asset reference of the wrapped tool for you. A `.uasset` suffix, an object suffix (`.WBP_Example`), backslashes, and the legacy `path` / `widgetBlueprintPath` / `widgetBlueprint` spellings are accepted and normalized. Create actions take `assetPath` too; `name` plus `packagePath` remains valid and is composed into it. See [Widget parameter contract](widget-parameters.md).

Call widget(action, args={...}). Actions:
